features.name: MBS User Service provisioning (Nmb10)
features.summary: The MBSF serves every resource and method of both Nmbsf APIs, with the required attributes, update rules (except that two attributes are also applied outside the INACTIVE state), conditional requests and notifications; the enhanced PATCH body that TS 29.580 V18.8.0 adds is later than the pinned V18.7.0 and is noted, not judged. Four of the sixteen status events are never raised, two are raised at a different point than the procedure gives, and the life-cycle differs at deactivation, at expiry and in when MBS System resources are reserved. The Application Provider portal uses both APIs with the required attributes, but sends response-only and immutable attributes in its requests, offers no form to add or remove a Distribution Session within an ingest session (its API passes such requests through), and connects without TLS.

requirements.name: Nmbsf_MBSUserService API (Nmb10)

cases.case: apiName and version nmbsf-mbs-us/v1
cases.what: Serves the API under nmbsf-mbs-us with version v1 and refuses any other version with 400.

cases.case: Retrieve all active MBS User Services (GET /mbs-user-services)
cases.what: Answers 200 with an array of MBSUserService, empty when none exist, leaving out services being deleted.

cases.case: Create (POST /mbs-user-services): 201, Location, body
cases.what: Creates the MBS User Service and answers 201 with an absolute Location URI of the new resource and the MBSUserService body; a non-JSON content type gets 415 and an unparsable body 400.

cases.case: Create: required attributes extServiceIds, servType, servClass, servAnnModes, servNameDescs
cases.what: The generated model refuses a body that lacks any of the five required attributes, and the handler answers it with 400 and the MANDATORY_IE_MISSING cause.

cases.case: servNameDescs entry carries servName or servDescrip
cases.what: Refuses a ServiceNameDescription that has neither a name nor a description.

cases.case: Retrieve (GET /mbs-user-services/{mbsUserServId}): 200, 404
cases.what: Answers 200 with the MBSUserService, an entity tag and Last-Modified, honours If-None-Match (304) and If-Match (412), and answers an unknown identifier with 404.

cases.case: Update (PUT): 200 or 204
cases.what: Replaces the representation after checking the target exists (404), the content type (415) and If-Match (412), and answers 200 with the updated MBSUserService.

cases.case: Modify (PATCH, application/merge-patch+json): 200 or 204
cases.what: Applies a JSON Merge Patch to the attributes MBSUserServicePatch carries, refuses any other patch media type with 415 and Accept-Patch, and answers 200 with the updated resource.

cases.case: servType not updated (PUT and PATCH)
cases.what: Refuses a PUT that changes servType and a PATCH that names servType, with 400.

cases.case: Delete (DELETE): 204
cases.what: Removes the MBS User Service together with its MBS User Data Ingest Sessions and answers 204 once removal completes; an unknown identifier gets 404.

cases.case: Method not served on a resource: 405 with Allow
cases.what: Answers PUT, PATCH and DELETE on the collection with 405 and an Allow header, and a method no resource serves with 501.

noted: A create whose servAnnModes asks for the User Service Announcement Channel is refused with 400 unless the MBSF has a local announcement channel configuration.
OPTIONS is answered on the collection and on an individual MBS User Service with 204 and an Allow header; TS 29.580 defines no OPTIONS.

requirements.name: Nmbsf_MBSUserDataIngestSession sessions (Nmb10)

cases.case: Retrieve all active sessions (GET /sessions)
cases.what: Answers 200 with an array of MBSUserDataIngSession, empty when there are none.

cases.case: Create (POST /sessions): 201, Location, body
cases.what: Creates the session and answers 201 with an absolute Location URI and the session body once the MB-SMF and MBSTF have answered for its MBS Distribution Sessions; content type, size and JSON errors are refused first.

cases.case: Create: required mbsUserServId and mbsDisSessInfos
cases.what: The generated model refuses a body without either attribute, and a parent MBS User Service that does not exist is refused with 400.

cases.case: actPeriods and actPeriodsRepRule mutually exclusive
cases.what: Refuses a create, update or patch that carries both, with 400 naming both attributes.

cases.case: TMGI requested when no mbsSessionId is provided
cases.what: Sets the TMGI request on the MBS Session it creates at the MB-SMF when mbsSessionId is absent, and uses a consumer-supplied TMGI as given.

cases.case: TMGI requested for an SSM with locationDependent true
cases.what: Also requests a TMGI when mbsSessionId carries an SSM and locationDependent is true.

cases.case: Retrieve (GET /sessions/{sessionId}): 200, 404
cases.what: Answers 200 with the session, an entity tag and Last-Modified, honours If-None-Match and If-Match, and answers an unknown identifier with 404.

cases.case: Update (PUT): 200 or 204
cases.what: Replaces the session after checking the target, If-Match, content type and body, and answers 200 with the updated representation once the MB-SMF and MBSTF have answered for any change.

cases.case: Modify (PATCH) with MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch (merge patch)
cases.what: Applies an application/merge-patch+json body against the stored representation, refuses attributes MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch does not carry, and answers 200.

cases.case: Modify (PATCH) with MBSUserDataIngSessionPatchEnh when MBSPatchEnh is supported
cases.what: The MBSF negotiates only features 2 and 3 (MBSEventsExt and MBSErrorHandling), so MBSPatchEnh is never agreed, and a PATCH body is parsed only as MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch from the pinned API 1.1.2, which has no MBSUserDataIngSessionPatchEnh.
cases.locator: TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 5.3.2.4.2 step 1; table 6.2.8-1, feature 4

cases.case: mbsSessionId, mbsDistSessionId and locationDependent never updated
cases.what: Refuses an update or patch that changes any of the three for an existing MBS Distribution Session.

cases.case: Other Distribution Session attributes updated only while INACTIVE
cases.what: Applies mbsServInfo, mbsFSAId and tgtServAreas at any time, as clause 5.3.2.4.2 allows, but also applies extTgtServAreas and nrRedCapUeInfo while the MBS Distribution Session is not INACTIVE; any other attribute change is refused unless the session is INACTIVE.

cases.case: Add a Distribution Session with a new map key
cases.what: A new key in mbsDisSessInfos creates a new MBS Distribution Session at the MB-SMF and MBSTF, and the update is answered once they have answered.

cases.case: Remove a Distribution Session with a NULL map entry
cases.what: On PUT, a key set to null in mbsDisSessInfos is taken out before validation and its MBS Distribution Session is torn down; on PATCH, the body is first checked as MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch, whose map values must be whole MBSDistributionSessionInfo objects, so a null entry is refused with 400 and nothing is removed.

cases.case: Delete (DELETE /sessions/{sessionId}): 204
cases.what: Deletes the session and its MBS Distribution Sessions at the MBSTF and answers 204 when the teardown completes, or at once when nothing is left to tear down; an unknown identifier gets 404.

noted: An MBS Distribution Session given an mbsSessionId already used by another session is refused with 400, or reported in failedDistSessions where MBSErrorHandling is negotiated.

mbsUserServiceAnmt is filled in the create response as well as in update responses when the service is provisioned PASSED_BACK and every Distribution Session is ESTABLISHED or ACTIVE; table 6.2.6.2.2-1 allows it only in a PUT or PATCH response.

TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 5.3.2.4.2 step 1 names MBSUserDataIngSessionPatchEnh as the PATCH body without condition, while the next sentence and table 6.2.3.3.3.3-2 make it conditional on MBSPatchEnh and keep MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch; Annex A.1 gives the OpenAPI precedence on encoding ("This Annex takes precedence when being discrepant to other parts of the specification with respect to the encoding of information elements and methods within the API(s)."), and its PATCH body is anyOf the two types, so the PATCH case with MBSUserDataIngSessionPatch is judged against that.

requirements.name: Nmbsf_MBSUserDataIngestSession status subscriptions and notifications

cases.case: Retrieve all subscriptions (GET /status-subscriptions)
cases.what: Answers 200 with an array of MBSUserDataIngStatSubsc, empty when there are none.

cases.case: Create (POST /status-subscriptions): 201, Location, body
cases.what: Creates the subscription and answers 201 with an absolute Location URI and the subscription body.

cases.case: Create: mbsIngSessionId, eventSubscs and notifUri required and checked
cases.what: The generated model refuses a body missing any of the three, and a subscription naming an unknown ingest session or Distribution Session is refused with 400.

cases.case: Retrieve (GET /status-subscriptions/{subscriptionId})
cases.what: Answers 200 with the subscription, honours If-None-Match and If-Match, and answers an unknown subscription with 404 and SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND.

cases.case: Update (PUT): only eventSubscs and notifUri change
cases.what: Replaces the subscription, refuses a change of mbsIngSessionId, and answers 200 with the subscription.

cases.case: Modify (PATCH, merge patch)
cases.what: Applies eventSubscs and notifUri from an application/merge-patch+json body through MBSUserDataIngStatSubscPatch and answers 200.

cases.case: Delete (DELETE): 204
cases.what: Removes the subscription and answers 204.

cases.case: StatusNotify: POST to notifUri with mbsIngSessionId and eventNotifs
cases.what: Sends a POST of MBSUserDataIngStatNotif (application/json) to the subscribed notifUri carrying the events that changed since the last report.

cases.case: Distribution Session level events reported with mbsDisSessionId
cases.what: Reports a Distribution Session level event only for a subscribed event naming mbsDistSessionId, and carries that identifier in the notification.

cases.case: MBSEventsExt events sent only when the feature is negotiated
cases.what: Leaves out SESSION_STARTED, SESSION_RELEASED, DIST_SESS_ACTIVATED, DIST_SESS_EST_FAILURE and USER_SER_AD unless MBSEventsExt was negotiated on the ingest session.

noted: A method other than GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or OPTIONS on an individual subscription is answered 400 rather than 405 with an Allow header.

requirements.name: MBS User Data Ingest Session status events

cases.case: Session started (SESSION_STARTED, from Nmb1)
cases.what: The event can be subscribed to but is never raised: MB-SMF notifications are logged and not turned into events.

cases.case: Session released (SESSION_RELEASED, from Nmb1)
cases.what: The event can be subscribed to but is never raised.

cases.case: User Data Ingest Session starting (USER_DATA_ING_SESS_STARTING)
cases.what: Raised when the ingest session is processed for start and sent to subscribers that asked for it.

cases.case: Distribution Session starting (DIST_SESS_STARTING)
cases.what: Raised when the MBSF sends the Nmb2 create for the MBS Distribution Session.

cases.case: Distribution Session starting carries the content ingest parameters chosen by the MBSTF
cases.what: The event is raised before the MBSTF answers and carries no additional information; the ingest parameters reach the Application Provider only in the session representation.

cases.case: Distribution Session establishment failure (DIST_SESS_EST_FAILURE)
cases.what: Raised, with the reason as additional information, when the Nmb2 create is not answered successfully.

cases.case: Distribution Session established (DIST_SESS_STARTED)
cases.what: Raised when the MBSTF answers the Nmb2 create, before the MBSTF reports that content ingest is established; clause 5.3 has it follow the MBSTF Distribution Session established event.

cases.case: Distribution Session service management failure (DIST_SESS_SERV_MNGT_FAILURE)
cases.what: Raised from an MBSTF SERVICE_MANAGEMENT_FAILURE report.

cases.case: Distribution Session policy control failure (DIST_SESS_POL_CRTL_FAILURE, from Nmb12)
cases.what: The event can be subscribed to but is never raised; the MBSF has no Nmb12 interaction.

cases.case: User Data delivery started (DELIVERY_STARTED, from Nmb1)
cases.what: The MB-SMF broadcast delivery status notification is logged and not turned into the event.

cases.case: Distribution Session activated (DIST_SESS_ACTIVATED)
cases.what: Raised from an MBSTF SESSION_ACTIVATED report.

cases.case: Distribution Session deactivated (DIST_SESS_TERMINATED)
cases.what: Raised from an MBSTF SESSION_DEACTIVATED report, and also when the MBSTF reports a data ingest or service management failure.

cases.case: User Data Ingest Session established (USER_DATA_ING_SESS_STARTED)
cases.what: Raised once every MBS Distribution Session of the ingest session is established.

cases.case: User data ingest failure (DATA_INGEST_FAILURE)
cases.what: Raised from an MBSTF DATA_INGEST_FAILURE report.

cases.case: User Data Ingest Session terminated (USER_DATA_ING_SESS_TERMINATED and SESSION_TERMINATED)
cases.what: Raised once every MBS Distribution Session of the ingest session is terminated, and SESSION_TERMINATED also from an MBSTF DATA_INGEST_SESSION_TERMINATED report.

cases.case: User Service advertisement (USER_SER_AD) carries the external service identifiers in unicast mode
cases.what: The notification carries the URL of the announcement bundle as additional information, not the external service identifiers.
cases.locator: clause 4.6.2, table 4.6.2-1, row User Service advertisement

cases.case: User Service advertisement (USER_SER_AD) carries a URL for MBS-1 in external delivery mode
cases.what: The event is raised only for a service carried on the User Service Announcement Channel, whose carousel object supplies the URL; a service provisioned PASSED_BACK without the channel is never sent the event.
cases.locator: clause 4.6.2, table 4.6.2-1, row User Service advertisement

requirements.name: MBS Distribution Session life-cycle in the MBSF

cases.case: Provisioned INACTIVE, with an INACTIVE replica created in the MBSTF
cases.what: Creates the MBS Distribution Session in the MBSTF at provisioning with the state the active periods give, which is INACTIVE before the pre-start window.

cases.case: End before start refused at provisioning
cases.what: An active period whose end precedes its start is accepted and stored; nothing compares the two.

cases.case: End in the past: the session expires and is no longer provisioned
cases.what: A window that has already ended is skipped and the session stays provisioned in the INACTIVE state.

cases.case: ESTABLISHED shortly before the start time
cases.what: Moves the session to ESTABLISHED a configured number of seconds before each start time and tells the MBSTF.

cases.case: MBS System resources reserved at the ESTABLISHED transition
cases.what: The MBS Session is created at the MB-SMF when the ingest session is provisioned, and later transitions only switch its activity status between active and inactive.

cases.case: ACTIVE at the start time, signalled to the MBSTF by an Nmb2 update
cases.what: At each start time sends an Nmb2 PATCH setting distSessionState to ACTIVE.

cases.case: Deactivation at the end time: update to DEACTIVATING
cases.what: At the end of an active period sends an Nmb2 PATCH setting the state to INACTIVE, not DEACTIVATING.

cases.case: Deactivation: release in the MBSTF and in the MBS System (steps 4c, 4d)
cases.what: At the end of an active period the MBSTF session is kept and the MBS Session is only marked inactive; neither is released until the ingest session is deleted.

cases.case: Severe MBSTF error: DEACTIVATING and the deactivation procedure
cases.what: A DATA_INGEST_FAILURE or SERVICE_MANAGEMENT_FAILURE report sets the session INACTIVE in the MBSF and is reported as deactivated, without the DEACTIVATING transition and steps 4a to 4d.

cases.case: Subscription to MBSTF status events
cases.what: Subscribes in the Nmb2 create itself, through distSessionSubscription, naming its notification URI and the event types; it issues no separate StatusSubscribe request.

cases.case: MBSTF notifications received and answered 204
cases.what: Accepts StatusNotify POSTs on its notification URI, records the reported events and answers 204.

cases.case: HTTP/2 for Nmbsf
cases.what: Nmbsf is served by the open5gs SBI server, whose nghttp2 server provides HTTP/2.

cases.case: application/json for bodies
cases.what: Refuses a POST or PUT body that is not application/json with 415 and sends JSON responses as application/json.

cases.case: application/merge-patch+json for PATCH
cases.what: Accepts only application/merge-patch+json on PATCH and refuses others with 415 and Accept-Patch.

cases.case: application/problem+json for errors
cases.what: Error responses carry a ProblemDetails body as application/problem+json with a cause.

requirements.name: MBS User Service provisioning by the Application Provider

cases.case: POST to {apiRoot}/nmbsf-mbs-us/v1/mbs-user-services
cases.what: The portal creates a service by sending POST to /nmbsf-mbs-us/v1/mbs-user-services on the configured MBSF host and port.

cases.case: extServiceIds included
cases.what: The form requires an external service identifier and sends it as a one-element extServiceIds array; the portal server refuses a missing, empty or blank-item array before sending.

cases.case: servType included
cases.what: The form sends servType chosen from MULTICAST or BROADCAST, and the server refuses a body without it.

cases.case: servClass included
cases.what: The form sends servClass from a required field that defaults to the OMA BCAST service class term, and the server refuses a body without it.

cases.case: servAnnModes included (at least one)
cases.what: The form sends the ticked announcement modes and refuses to submit with none ticked; the server also refuses an empty list.

cases.case: servNameDescs included, each entry with language
cases.what: The form sends one servNameDescs entry carrying language, and the server refuses a missing list or any entry without language.
cases.locator: TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 6.1.6.2.3, table 6.1.6.2.3-1, row language

cases.case: each servNameDescs entry carries at least one of servName and servDescrip
cases.what: The form always sends both servName and servDescrip in the entry, so at least one is always present.

cases.case: mainServLang optional
cases.what: The form sends mainServLang set to the same language as the name and description entry.

cases.case: Retrieve an individual MBS User Service with GET
cases.what: The portal reads a service with GET on /nmbsf-mbs-us/v1/mbs-user-services/{id}, with the identifier encoded as one path segment.

cases.case: Update with PUT carrying a full MBSUserService
cases.what: Saving an open service sends PUT with the full MBSUserService body, which the server checks for the same mandatory attributes as on creation.

cases.case: Update with PATCH as JSON Merge Patch
cases.what: The portal's own API forwards a PATCH body to the MBSF with Content-Type application/merge-patch+json; the bundled web form does not offer PATCH.

cases.case: servType is never changed by an update
cases.what: The edit form keeps the service type selectable and sends whatever is selected on PUT, so the portal can ask for a servType change and leaves refusal to the MBSF; the clause allows no servType update.

cases.case: Delete with DELETE, 204 No Content handled
cases.what: Deleting a service sends DELETE on the individual resource and treats any 2xx (204 included) as success, after first deleting the ingest sessions and status subscriptions the portal created under it.

cases.case: Location header of the 201 response used to identify the created resource
cases.what: The portal takes the service identifier from the last path segment of the Location header, records it, and passes the header back to the page, which opens the new service from it.

noted: The portal never calls GET on the MBS User Services collection: it lists the services it created itself from a local registry, refreshing each one with the individual GET and dropping any that answer 404. Its own comments say the running MBSF answers 400 to the collection GET.
No suppFeat is sent on MBSUserService. TS 29.580 V18.8.0 table 6.1.8-1 lists no features for this API, so no feature negotiation applies.
When the name and description fields are both left blank, the entry is sent with servName and servDescrip as empty strings; this meets the schema's anyOf but carries neither a name nor a description.

Deleting a service first deletes the ingest sessions and status subscriptions the portal recorded under it. No clause requires this; the portal does it because it does not rely on the MBSF's own cascade.

Three of the four example templates in rt-mbs-examples (single-file-download, carousel-file-set, packet-forwarding) have a service block without servAnnModes, so creating their service through the portal is refused by its own mandatory-field check.

requirements.name: MBS User Data Ingest Session provisioning by the Application Provider

cases.case: POST to {apiRoot}/nmbsf-mbs-ud-ingest/v1/sessions
cases.what: The portal creates an ingest session by sending POST to /nmbsf-mbs-ud-ingest/v1/sessions on the MBSF.

cases.case: mbsUserServId included
cases.what: The form fills mbsUserServId with the service currently selected, and the server refuses a body without it.

cases.case: mbsDisSessInfos map with at least one entry
cases.what: The form sends mbsDisSessInfos as a map with one entry under a caller-chosen key (default AP_MBS_SESSION_1), and the server refuses an empty map.

cases.case: Each entry carries distrMethod and maxContBitRate
cases.what: Every entry built by the form or a template carries distrMethod and maxContBitRate, and the server refuses an entry missing either.

cases.case: Exactly one of objDistrInfo and pckDistrInfo
cases.what: The form builds only the parameter set that matches the chosen distribution method, never both.

cases.case: objDistrInfo carries operatingMode, objAcqMethod and objAcqIds
cases.what: For the object method the form always sends operatingMode, objAcqMethod and objAcqIds (possibly an empty list), and the server refuses an objDistrInfo missing any of them.

cases.case: objAcqIds value determined as TS 26.502 clause 6.1 requires
cases.what: The form sends whatever identifiers are typed, an empty list included, for every operating mode and acquisition method, and neither the form nor the portal server checks the list against TS 26.502 V18.6.0 table 6.1-1 (one or more identifiers for PULL OBJECT_SINGLE, an empty set for PUSH OBJECT_SINGLE, a single manifest URL for OBJECT_COLLECTION).

cases.case: objIngUri sent by the Application Provider for PULL only
cases.what: objIngUri is added only when the acquisition method is PULL; for PUSH it is left for the MBSF to return.

cases.case: pckDistrInfo carries operatingMode, pckIngMethod and ingEndpointAddrs
cases.what: For the packet method the form sends all three and refuses to submit without an ingest endpoint address; the server refuses a pckDistrInfo missing any of them.

cases.case: pckIngMethod is UNICAST when operatingMode is PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY
cases.what: Choosing PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY disables the MULTICAST option and forces UNICAST.
cases.locator: TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 6.2.6.2.6, table 6.2.6.2.6-1, row pckIngMethod

cases.case: actPeriods or actPeriodsRepRule, never both
cases.what: Active periods are sent at the ingest-session level, and the form refuses a body that carries both actPeriods and actPeriodsRepRule.

cases.case: suppFeat signals the features the body relies on
cases.what: Every ingest session is sent with suppFeat "3", which signals features 1 (5MBS2, needed for actPeriodsRepRule and the Rel-18 fields) and 2 (MBSEventsExt, needed for USER_SER_AD and the other extended events).

cases.case: mbsSessionId optional for a broadcast service (TMGI nominated or left to the MBSF)
cases.what: Under a BROADCAST service the form sends a TMGI when a service ID is typed and omits mbsSessionId otherwise, leaving TMGI allocation to the MBSF.

cases.case: mbsDistSessState not sent in requests
cases.what: The form sends mbsDistSessState in every create and PUT body unless Active periods or a repetition rule are given, and uses it as the activation control; the clause makes it a response-only attribute.
cases.locator: TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 6.2.6.2.3, table 6.2.6.2.3-1, row mbsDistSessState

cases.case: mbsDistSessionId not sent in requests
cases.what: On PUT the form echoes back the mbsDistSessionId it loaded, because the running MBSF refuses a PUT without it; the clause makes it a response-only attribute.
cases.locator: TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 6.2.6.2.3, table 6.2.6.2.3-1, row mbsDistSessionId

cases.case: objRepairUri not sent in requests
cases.what: For PULL sessions the form sends objRepairUri when the field is filled; the clause allows it only in responses.
cases.locator: TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 6.2.6.2.5, table 6.2.6.2.5-1, row objRepairUri

cases.case: tgtServAreas and extTgtServAreas not both
cases.what: Both fields are free JSON inputs and both are sent when both are filled; nothing refuses the combination.

cases.case: Retrieve an individual ingest session with GET
cases.what: The portal reads a session with GET on /nmbsf-mbs-ud-ingest/v1/sessions/{id}.

cases.case: Update with PUT carrying a full MBSUserDataIngSession
cases.what: Saving an open session sends PUT with mbsUserServId, mbsDisSessInfos, suppFeat and any active periods, checked for the same mandatory attributes as on creation.

cases.case: Update with PATCH as JSON Merge Patch
cases.what: The portal's own API forwards a PATCH body unchanged to the MBSF with Content-Type application/merge-patch+json; the bundled web form does not offer PATCH.

cases.case: PATCH body MBSUserDataIngSessionPatchEnh when MBSPatchEnh is supported
cases.what: Every ingest session is sent with suppFeat "3" (features 1 and 2), so MBSPatchEnh (feature 4) is never signalled; the portal has no MBSUserDataIngSessionPatchEnh body of its own and its PATCH API forwards the caller's body as given.
cases.locator: TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 5.3.2.4.2 step 1; table 6.2.8-1, feature 4

cases.case: mbsSessionId and mbsDistSessionId never changed by an update
cases.what: On PUT the form sends back exactly the mbsSessionId and mbsDistSessionId it loaded and disables the SSM fields of an existing session.

cases.case: locationDependent never changed by an update
cases.what: The Location dependent checkbox stays editable on an existing session and its current state is sent on PUT, so the portal can ask to change an attribute the clause makes immutable.

cases.case: Other Distribution Session attributes updated only while INACTIVE
cases.what: The edit form lets every non-identity field be changed and sent on PUT whatever the session's current state, leaving refusal to the MBSF.

cases.case: Add a Distribution Session to an existing ingest session with a new map key
cases.what: The portal's own API forwards a PUT or PATCH body carrying a new mbsDisSessInfos map key unchanged to the MBSF; the bundled web form and templates edit one entry per session and offer no way to add a second.

cases.case: Remove a Distribution Session with a NULL map entry
cases.what: The portal's own PATCH API forwards a body with a mbsDisSessInfos entry set to null unchanged to the MBSF as JSON Merge Patch; its PUT path refuses a null entry, and the bundled web form offers neither, so from the form a Distribution Session can only be removed by deleting the whole ingest session.

cases.case: Delete with DELETE, 204 No Content handled
cases.what: Deleting a session sends DELETE on the individual resource after deleting the status subscriptions the portal recorded for it, and treats any 2xx as success.

cases.case: Location header of the 201 response used to identify the created session
cases.what: The portal takes the session identifier from the Location header, records it under its parent service, and the page opens the session from it.

noted: Under a MULTICAST service the form always sends an SSM pair as mbsSessionId; it cannot nominate a TMGI or leave the identifier to the MBSF. TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 5.3 step 3 makes TMGI nomination optional, so this is a limitation, not a failed case.
The template loader builds an SSM mbsSessionId for every template session, including under a BROADCAST service, unlike the form.
When active periods are given, the form removes mbsDistSessState from every entry because the MBSF refuses the combination. That rule comes from the MBSF's own message, not from a clause read here.

The form edits only the first map entry of a session; a PUT of a session that holds several Distribution Sessions sends only that one entry. TS 29.580 says removal is by a NULL entry and does not say, in the clauses read, what a PUT omitting an entry does.
The code comment on the PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY rule cites 'TS 29.580 V18.8.0, table 5.6.2.8-1'; the sentence it quotes is in table 6.2.6.2.6-1 of that document.
The read-only announcement URL field shows mbsUserServiceAnmtUrl when the MBSF returns it.

requirements.name: Status subscription and notifications at the Application Provider

cases.case: POST {apiRoot}/nmbsf-mbs-ud-ingest/v1/status-subscriptions with mbsIngSessionId, eventSubscs and notifUri
cases.what: Subscribing from an open ingest session sends POST to /nmbsf-mbs-ud-ingest/v1/status-subscriptions with that session's identifier, the ticked events and the notification URI; the server refuses a body missing any of the three or an event without statusEvent.

cases.case: Subscribed events drawn from the Event enumeration
cases.what: The offered events are the sixteen values of the Event enumeration, USER_SER_AD included.

cases.case: Modify a subscription with PUT or PATCH
cases.what: The portal's own API forwards PUT (full body, checked for the three mandatory attributes) and PATCH (as application/merge-patch+json) to the individual subscription; the bundled web form offers neither.

cases.case: Delete a subscription
cases.what: The portal sends DELETE on the individual subscription, directly or when its ingest session is deleted.

cases.case: Notification endpoint accepts POST of MBSUserDataIngStatNotif
cases.what: The portal listens for POST on its notification path, reads mbsIngSessionId and each eventNotifs entry, and keeps the last 50 events for the page.

cases.case: Notification answered with 204 No Content
cases.what: Every notification POST is answered 204 with no body.

cases.case: USER_SER_AD notification received and its information kept
cases.what: A USER_SER_AD notification is stored like any other and shown highlighted on the page with its statusAddInfo text; nothing parses that text further.
cases.locator: TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 6.2.6.3.4, table 6.2.6.3.4-1, row USER_SER_AD

cases.case: Retrieval of the composite announcement at MBS-1 using the URL from USER_SER_AD
cases.what: No code fetches the announcement from the URL a USER_SER_AD notification carries.

requirements.exists: The notification text, which for USER_SER_AD can carry the announcement URL (TS 26.517 V18.6.0 clause 8A.2), is shown on the page.
noted: MBS-8 (the provider telling the MBS-Aware Application about the service) is beyond the scope of 3GPP specification (TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 4.4.1, MBS-8 item), so no verdict is given. The portal has no MBS-8 path; in the examples the dashboard learns the service from the MBS Client instead.
PUT and PATCH on a subscription are forwarded as given; the portal does not check that only eventSubscs and notifUri change (TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clause 5.3.2.7.2 step 1).

The default notification URI in the form is http://127.0.0.1:8000/notifications, while the portal listens on port 8081 by default (8091 in the demo scripts); the /config route that reports the notification path is not used by the page. A subscription made with the default URI does not reach this portal. The example templates carry the same port 8000 URI.
The demo provisioning scripts create the service and ingest session through the portal but never create a status subscription, so in the demo the portal receives no notifications.
The optional mbsSessionId of an EventNotification is not kept.

requirements.name: HTTP usage towards the MBSF (Nmb10)

cases.case: HTTP/2 used by the provider's client
cases.what: Every Nmb10 request goes over Node's HTTP/2 client with prior knowledge, one connection per request.

cases.case: TLS available on the Nmb10 connection
cases.what: The client opens only cleartext HTTP/2 connections (http scheme) and has no option for HTTPS; the clause requires every NF to support TLS.

cases.case: Content-Type application/json on POST and PUT bodies
cases.what: Any request with a body is sent with Content-Type application/json unless the caller overrides it.

cases.case: Content-Type application/merge-patch+json on PATCH
cases.what: All three PATCH operations pass application/merge-patch+json as the content type.

cases.case: User-Agent identifying the NF type on every request
cases.what: No User-Agent header is set on Nmb10 requests (a recommendation in the clause, not a requirement, for direct communication).
cases.locator: TS 29.500 V18.10.0 clause 5.2.2.2, table 5.2.2.2-1, row User-Agent

noted: OAuth2 access to both Nmbsf APIs is optional, 'based on local configuration' (TS 29.580 V18.8.0 clauses 6.1.9 and 6.2.9); the portal has no support for it, so it can only be used where the MBSF does not require it.
Requests time out after 30 s by default (MBSF_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS) because the MBSF delays its answer to DELETE until the MBSTF confirms. The bound is an operator setting; no clause gives one.
A non-JSON response body from the MBSF is reported as an error (502 to the page) rather than parsed.

features.name: MBS Distribution Sessions (Nmb2)
features.summary: The MBSTF serves every method of the Nmbstf API with its notifications, and the MBSF creates, updates, deletes and subscribes to MBS Distribution Sessions with it; the MBSTF returns no expiry time it chose, keeps notifying an old URI after a subscription update, reports deactivation and ingest establishment at the wrong moments, waits for the MBSF before attempting ingest and keeps accepting pushed objects when INACTIVE, and the specifications disagree on the API name spelling and who nominates the push ingest URL.

requirements.name: Nmbstf_MBSDistributionSession API (Nmb2)

cases.case: Create: POST /dist-sessions answered 201 with a Location header and a CreateRspData body
cases.what: A POST on the collection builds the session from CreateReqData, answers 201 Created with a Location header naming /dist-sessions/{distSessionRef} and a body that is CreateRspData wrapping the created DistSession, and refuses a body that is not application/json with 415.

cases.case: Update: PATCH /dist-sessions/{distSessionRef} takes array(PatchItem) as a JSON Patch document (table 6.1.3.3.3.1-2)
cases.what: The PATCH handler refuses any media type other than application/json-patch+json with the Accept-Patch header, applies the JSON Patch operations to the DistSession representation (the GET representation), and rejects a patch that changes distSessionId or the operating mode or asks for a state transition the life-cycle does not allow.

cases.case: Update: success answered 200 with DistSession (or 204)
cases.what: A successful update is always answered 200 OK with the updated DistSession as the body (not the CreateRspData wrapper), which is one of the two success responses the clause allows.

cases.case: Retrieve: GET /dist-sessions/{distSessionRef} answered 200 with DistSession
cases.what: A GET answers 200 OK with the DistSession representation as application/json, and 406 when the Accept header excludes application/json.

cases.case: Destroy: DELETE /dist-sessions/{distSessionRef} answered 204
cases.what: A DELETE removes the session from the context, which tears down its controller and its ingest and output, and answers 204 No Content.

cases.case: StatusSubscribe: POST .../subscriptions answered 201 with a Location header and StatusSubscribeRspData carrying the subscribed events
cases.what: A POST on the subscriptions collection creates the subscription with an MBSTF-assigned UUID, answers 201 Created with a Location header for the new subscription and a StatusSubscribeRspData body whose subscription echoes the accepted eventList, plus any immediate event reports.

cases.case: StatusSubscribe: response carries the expiry time after which the subscription becomes invalid
cases.what: The response echoes expiryTime only when the consumer sent one; when the request has none the MBSTF neither chooses nor returns an expiry time, whereas the clause requires the response to include it.

cases.case: StatusSubscribe: response carries the Distribution Session Identifier
cases.what: The response is StatusSubscribeRspData as the OpenAPI definition gives it (subscription and optional reportList), with no distribution session identifier, which that data type has no attribute for.

cases.case: Subscription update: PATCH .../subscriptions/{subscriptionId} answered 200 with DistSessionSubscription
cases.what: The PATCH refuses media types other than application/json-patch+json, applies each PatchItem to the stored DistSessionSubscription, recomputes the event filter and the expiry timer, and answers 200 OK with the updated DistSessionSubscription.

cases.case: Subscription update: a changed expiryTime takes effect
cases.what: After a patch the expiry timer is cancelled and rescheduled from the new expiryTime, so the subscription is removed at the new time.

cases.case: Subscription update: a changed notifyUri takes effect
cases.what: The new notifyUri is stored and used as the request URI, but the HTTP client created for the first notification is kept, so once a notification has been sent later notifications still connect to the address of the original notifyUri when the new one names a different host or port.

cases.case: StatusUnsubscribe: DELETE .../subscriptions/{subscriptionId} answered 204
cases.what: A DELETE removes the subscription (cancelling its expiry timer) and answers 204 No Content.

cases.case: Unknown distribution session or subscription answered 404
cases.what: A distSessionRef or subscriptionId that does not exist is answered 404 with a ProblemDetails body carrying an invalid parameter entry, for every method on the individual resources and the subscriptions collection.
cases.locator: clause 6.1.3.3.3.3, table 6.1.3.3.3.3-3, NOTE 1 (404 listed in TS29581_Nmbstf_DistSession.yaml for every operation)

cases.case: Required DistSession attributes enforced (distSessionId, distSessionState, mbUpfTunAddr, mbr)
cases.what: The generated model rejects a create or patch whose DistSession lacks any mandatory attribute (write-only ones such as mbUpfTunAddr and mbr are required in requests) with 400 MANDATORY_IE_MISSING, and hand-written checks add the conditional rules: exactly one of objDistributionData or pktDistributionData, and upTrafficFlowInfo (with srcIpAddr and transportSessionId for objects) where the table makes it conditional.

cases.case: Write-only attributes are not returned in responses
cases.what: Responses are serialised in response mode, in which the generated model omits attributes marked Write-Only (mbUpfTunAddr, mbr, upTrafficFlowInfo, dscpMarking, notifyUri and others) and emits Read-Only ones such as mbStfListenAddr and distSessionSubscUri.

cases.case: distSessionRef assigned by the MBSTF during Create
cases.what: The resource reference is the MBSF-assigned distSessionId itself, and a second create with an identifier already in use is refused with 400; since distSessionId is only unique within one MBS User Service, two User Services that use the same identifier cannot both be provisioned in one MBSTF.

cases.case: apiName nmbstf-distsession
cases.what: The MBSTF serves the API only under the lower-case name nmbstf-distsession; a request using the mixed-case name in the resource URI definitions is passed on as an unknown service.
cases.conflict: TS 29.581 V18.6.0 clause 6.1.1: "-The <apiName> shall be "nmbstf-distsession"." TS 29.581 V18.6.0 clause 6.1.3.2.2 (also 6.1.3.3.2 and 6.1.3.4.2): "Resource URI: {apiRoot}/nmbstf-distSession/<apiVersion>/dist-sessions"

cases.case: apiVersion v1
cases.what: Any API version other than v1 is refused with 400 INVALID_API before the resource is looked at.

cases.case: HTTP/2 used for the API (clause 6.1.2.1)
cases.what: The API is served by the Open5GS SBI server, which speaks HTTP/2; the shipped configuration runs it without TLS.

cases.case: Bodies signalled as application/json
cases.what: Success bodies are sent with Content-Type application/json and POST requests are required to carry application/json.

cases.case: Errors carry ProblemDetails as application/problem+json
cases.what: Error responses are built as ProblemDetails and sent with the problem content type.

noted: POST requests are refused with 415 unless the Content-Type header is exactly "application/json", so a media type with a parameter (for example a charset) is refused.
OPTIONS is served on every resource with an Allow list, and methods no resource of the API serves are answered 501; this goes beyond table 6.1.3.1-1.
An unknown distribution session is answered 404 with the cause SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND, a cause defined for subscriptions; TS 29.581 table 6.1.7.3-1 defines no application error for this.
An Update may change any attribute in any state (the running session is reconfigured), and the subscription PATCH also accepts a single PatchItem object rather than an array.
A subscription whose expiryTime is already in the past is created, answered 201 and removed at once; the expiry string is parsed only in the form YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ.
mbmsGwTunAddr and maxDelay are accepted and stored but never read.

TS 29.581 V18.6.0 clause 5.2.2.6.2 step 2a lists "the Distribution Session Identifier" in StatusSubscribeRspData, which table 6.1.6.2.8-1 and Annex A define with only subscription and reportList. Annex A.1 settles it: "This Annex takes precedence when being discrepant to other parts of the specification with respect to the encoding of information elements and methods within the API(s)." The case is judged on Annex A. Raised by the A5 reader, 2026-10-03.

On the API name, the OpenAPI file of Annex A (servers url {apiRoot}/nmbstf-distsession/v1) agrees with clause 6.1.1; the resource URIs of clauses 6.1.3.2.2 to 6.1.3.4.2 spell it nmbstf-distSession. The case stays inconsistent because a resource URI is not plainly an information element or method encoding, the scope of the Annex A.1 precedence rule.

requirements.name: Nmbstf StatusNotify

cases.case: POST to the subscribed notifyUri with StatusNotifyReqData (reportList)
cases.what: Each subscription sends a POST to its notifyUri with a StatusNotifyReqData body holding a DistSessionEventReportList of the events newer than those it last reported, each with eventType and timeStamp; 307/308 are followed once, 5xx are retried within a configured budget and 4xx are not repeated.

cases.case: notifyCorrelationId echoed when given at subscription
cases.what: The report list carries the subscription's notifyCorrelationId when one was given.

cases.case: DATA_INGEST_FAILURE sent when the MBSTF failed to ingest data
cases.what: Reported for every failed object pull (timeout, error status, missing Content-Type) and every refused object push; the Packet Distribution Method has no ingest-failure detection, so no packet-mode session ever reports it.

cases.case: SESSION_DEACTIVATED sent when the session is deactivated
cases.what: Recorded on every entry to the INACTIVE state, which includes the creation of every session (so a subscription made with the create request is told the session was deactivated before it was ever active) and a return from ESTABLISHED; it is also recorded when a session is destroyed, by which time the subscriptions it would be sent to are being removed. The report after DEACTIVATING completes is the one the clause describes.

cases.case: SESSION_ACTIVATED sent when the session is activated
cases.what: Recorded when the session enters ACTIVE, right after the output (packager or packet scheduler) has been started.

cases.case: SERVICE_MANAGEMENT_FAILURE sent when the session failed to start
cases.what: Recorded when the object packager reports a packaging failure (FEC configuration rejected, FLUTE transmitter could not be created, carousel exceeds the maximum bit rate) and when the push ingest server could not be started at creation; the packaging failure also requests the session to go INACTIVE.

cases.case: DATA_INGEST_SESSION_ESTABLISHED sent when the User Data Ingest Session is successfully established
cases.what: Recorded as soon as the session enters ESTABLISHED, immediately after the pull ingesters are created (object) or the packet socket is started (packet), without waiting for any object to be retrieved or packet received, so it is sent whether or not ingest succeeds.

cases.case: DATA_INGEST_SESSION_TERMINATED sent when the User Data Ingest Session is stopped at the end of the active period
cases.what: Recorded when a DEACTIVATING session has emptied its transmission queue, just before it moves to INACTIVE and its ingest is stopped.

cases.case: Events filtered to the subscription's eventList
cases.what: Each subscription keeps a bit mask built from its eventList and reports only those event types.

cases.case: Subscription expiry honoured
cases.what: A timer set from expiryTime removes the subscription when it passes, so no further notifications are generated for it.

noted: Only the latest time of each event type is kept, so several occurrences of the same event between two notifications are reported once.
The number of notification retries after a 5xx and the wait between them are operator configuration (notifyRetryAttempts, notifyRetryDelay, default 5 and 5 s).

requirements.name: MBS Distribution Session life-cycle in the MBSTF

cases.case: Created in INACTIVE
cases.what: Every new session enters the INACTIVE state first and stays there when the create request gives INACTIVE; a create asking for a later state is walked through the intermediate states to it.

cases.case: The MBSTF attempts ingest establishment after creation; ESTABLISHED on success, stays INACTIVE on failure
cases.what: The state follows only what the MBSF requests: a pull-based object session created INACTIVE makes no ingest attempt until the MBSF asks for ESTABLISHED, and entering ESTABLISHED does not depend on any object having been retrieved or packet received, so a failed ingest never leaves the session in INACTIVE.

cases.case: In ESTABLISHED the MBSTF may ingest but does not distribute
cases.what: Pull ingesters run from ESTABLISHED, but the object packager and the packet scheduler are only created when the session enters ACTIVE.

cases.case: ACTIVE starts sending MBS data packets to the MB-UPF (Nmb9)
cases.what: Entering ACTIVE creates or reactivates the FLUTE packager (object) or the packetiser and rate scheduler (packet), and queues the objects already ingested.

cases.case: DEACTIVATING ceases sending
cases.what: A request for DEACTIVATING (or INACTIVE) first empties the packaging queue, then stops the packet path at once or lets the FLUTE transmitter finish only the objects it already holds before deactivating, after which the session moves to INACTIVE.

cases.case: Release returns the session to INACTIVE and stops ingest at Nmb8
cases.what: On return to INACTIVE the pull ingesters are removed and the packet socket is stopped, but a push-based object session keeps its push ingest server open and keeps accepting objects until the session is destroyed.

cases.case: Destroy stops ingest
cases.what: Deleting the session destroys its controller, which aborts the push and pull ingesters and the object store worker, or closes the packet ingester.

cases.case: Activation acknowledged with the Distribution Session activated event (5.5.1 step 4)
cases.what: SESSION_ACTIVATED is recorded when the session enters ACTIVE and sent to the subscribers that asked for it.

cases.case: Deactivation acknowledged with the Distribution Session deactivated event (5.5.4 step 19)
cases.what: After DEACTIVATING has drained its queue the session moves to INACTIVE and records SESSION_DEACTIVATED (see US-D02 for the same event also being recorded at creation).

cases.case: Push-based object acquisition: the Create response carries the object ingest base URL, unique within the MBS System
cases.what: For push the MBSTF starts its push ingest server at creation and writes its own URL (host, port and a per-session path segment or ephemeral port) into objIngestBaseUrl, replacing any value the MBSF supplied, and the Create response carries it; the value is unique within this MBSTF.
cases.conflict: TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 5.3, step 10: "-In the case of the Object Distribution Method with push-based Object acquisition method, the response includes additional content ingest parameters chosen by the MBSTF for this MBS Distribution Session (see Object ingest base URL in table 4.5.62)." TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-2, row Object ingest base URL: "In this case, the value shall be nominated by the MBSF and shall be unique for all MBS Distribution Sessions within the MBS System."

cases.case: Packet distribution: the Create response carries the MBSTF ingest endpoint addresses
cases.what: For unicast ingest the ingest socket is opened while the session is set up, before the response is built, and its local address is written into mbStfIngressTunAddr (forward-only) or mbStfListenAddr (proxy), which the Create response returns.

noted: A SINGLE pull session moves itself to INACTIVE once every listed object has been fetched, and any session moves to INACTIVE after a configured number of consecutive ingest failures (consecutiveIngestFailuresBeforeDeactivate, default 5); TS 26.502 clause 5.5.1 step 9 allows the second for a severe fault.
Update refuses INACTIVE to DEACTIVATING, ESTABLISHED to DEACTIVATING and ACTIVE to ESTABLISHED as invalid transitions.

requirements.name: Nmbstf consumer requests from the MBSF (Nmb2)

cases.case: Create: POST /dist-sessions with CreateReqData
cases.what: Sends a POST of CreateReqData carrying a DistSession with distSessionId, distSessionState, mbUpfTunAddr, mbr, upTrafficFlowInfo and the object or packet distribution data.

cases.case: Update: PATCH with a JSON Patch on the DistSession
cases.what: Sends an application/json-patch+json PATCH replacing either /distSessionState or the whole DistSession.

cases.case: Destroy: DELETE /dist-sessions/{distSessionRef}
cases.what: Sends a DELETE on the MBS Distribution Session when it or its ingest session is removed.

cases.case: Object distribution data per operating mode and acquisition method
cases.what: Sends objAcquisitionIdsPull for PULL and objAcquisitionIdPush only for PUSH with a manifest mode, with the ingest and distribution base URLs.

cases.case: Packet distribution data
cases.what: Sends pktDistributionOperatingMode, pktIngestMethod and mbStfIngestAddr for a PACKET session.

cases.case: Traffic marking and FEC passed to the MBSTF
cases.what: Copies trafficMarkingInfo to dscpMarking, fecConfig to fecInformation and maxContDelay to maxDelay.

features.name: Object and packet distribution (Nmb8, MBS-4-MC)
features.summary: The MBSTF ingests objects by pull and push in all four operating modes, handles object manifests, forwards packets in proxy and forward-only mode, and sends towards the MB-UPF tunnel at the configured rate with User-Agent MBSTF on pulls; collections are refetched instead of sent once, manifest refetch rules differ, the FDT describes only the objects handed to the transmitter, an empty ingest base URL leaves pulls unfetched, and DSCP marking, packet FEC, TLS and the Server header on the push endpoint are absent. The Application Provider side relies on a mock origin for pull and pushes without TLS. FLUTE/ALC itself is in rt-libflute, audited separately.

requirements.name: Object Distribution Method operating modes

cases.case: OBJECT_SINGLE pull with one or more object URLs
cases.what: A SINGLE pull session without at least one objAcquisitionIdsPull entry is refused, and each listed URL becomes one pull ingest item (resolved against objIngestBaseUrl when one is given) that is distributed once and removed from the store after sending.

cases.case: Pull acquisition identifiers resolved to fetch URLs
cases.what: Relative identifiers are appended to objIngestBaseUrl; when objIngestBaseUrl is absent the fetch URL is left empty, so the object is never retrieved, and an absolute identifier given with an objIngestBaseUrl is dropped. The same construction is used for the manifest of COLLECTION, CAROUSEL and STREAMING sessions.
cases.locator: TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-2, row Object ingest base URL

cases.case: OBJECT_SINGLE push with empty acquisition identifiers
cases.what: A SINGLE push session that carries objAcquisitionIdPush is refused; with none, every object pushed to the session's ingest URL is accepted and distributed once.

cases.case: OBJECT_COLLECTION: a single object manifest URL
cases.what: COLLECTION and CAROUSEL sessions are refused unless exactly one pull identifier (pull) or one push identifier (push) is given, also on update; STREAMING accepts one pull identifier per supported entry-point type.

cases.case: OBJECT_COLLECTION: objects listed in the manifest are pulled and distributed once
cases.what: The listed objects are pulled and queued, but every object is kept after sending and is fetched again when its cache lifetime ends (10 s when the origin gives none) or after keepUpdatedInterval; each refetch, including a 304, raises an update event that queues the object for transmission again, so objects are distributed repeatedly.

cases.case: OBJECT_COLLECTION and OBJECT_CAROUSEL push mode: only the manifest is pushed, the objects are pulled
cases.what: In push mode a pushed object is accepted only at the path given by objAcquisitionIdPush (anything else is answered 400), and the objects the manifest lists are fetched by the pull workers.

cases.case: OBJECT_CAROUSEL: distributed according to the repetition pattern in the manifest
cases.what: Each carousel item is rescheduled after its repetitionInterval, and items without one share the bit rate left over within mbr; a carousel needing more than mbr is reported as a packaging failure.

cases.case: OBJECT_CAROUSEL: a changed object is reflected at the next opportunity
cases.what: A refetched object that changed replaces the queued carousel item and is sent on its next repetition.

cases.case: OBJECT_CAROUSEL: replacement object manifest
cases.what: A new manifest is merged into the current one, objects it no longer lists are removed from the carousel and the store, and new ones are scheduled for fetching.

cases.case: OBJECT_STREAMING: a single Application Service Entry Point URL of each type
cases.what: A STREAMING session takes between one and as many identifiers as there are streaming manifest types implemented (one: DASH MPD).

cases.case: OBJECT_STREAMING: the DASH MPD is used to update the object list
cases.what: The DASH handler lists the segments each MPD makes available, schedules each for fetching at its availability start time and records its availability start and end times on the ingested object.

cases.case: OBJECT_STREAMING: an updated MPD reflected at the soonest opportunity
cases.what: The MPD is refetched at its minimumUpdatePeriod (pull) or accepted when pushed, replaces the current MPD when it differs, and is itself resent at the configured mpdRepetitionRate.

cases.case: OBJECT_STREAMING: last packet of each object at the MBSTF Client no later than its availability start time
cases.what: Each segment is fetched only at the availability start time the MPD gives (past times are moved to now), and that same time is used as its transmission deadline with no distribution offset added, so transmission necessarily completes after it.

noted: The MBSTF has no Object Repair configuration of its own (no repair attribute reaches it in DistSession), so the rule that repair is not used with OBJECT_STREAMING (TS 26.517 clause 6.2.3.1) gives it nothing to do.

TS 26.502 V18.6.0 table 6.1-1 row OBJECT_STREAMING says the content type of each Application Service Entry Point "shall be explicitly indicated", but TS 29.581 V18.6.0 table 6.1.6.2.5-1 gives objAcquisitionIdsPull no attribute to carry it, so the MBSTF cannot receive it at Nmb2. This is a gap at stage 3, not a contradiction, and the sentence binds whoever provisions the session, so no verdict is given. The MBSTF takes the type from the Content-Type the origin returns.

requirements.name: Object ingest at Nmb8

cases.case: Pull-based ingest of objects from the origin
cases.what: Pull ingesters fetch each item with libcurl (conditional requests with If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since on refetch, redirects followed), store the body with its Content-Type, ETag, Last-Modified and cache lifetime, and refuse a 2xx response that carries no Content-Type.

cases.case: Push-based ingest endpoint receiving objects
cases.what: A libmicrohttpd server per session (or one shared port with a per-session path segment) accepts PUT, POST and PUSH requests, refuses other methods with 405 and objects without a Content-Type with 400, and stores accepted objects under their pushed URL.

cases.case: Object ingest base URL replaced by the object distribution base URL before distribution
cases.what: When both base URLs are known and the fetched URL starts with the ingest base URL, the Content-Location handed to FLUTE is the distribution base URL followed by the rest of the URL.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-2, row Object ingest base URL

cases.case: Nothing substituted when the base URLs are omitted
cases.what: Without both base URLs the fetched (or pushed) URL is used unchanged as the Content-Location.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-2, row Object ingest base URL

cases.case: Content type of ingested objects verified against the acquisition identifier's content type
cases.what: No ingested object's Content-Type is compared with a content type given for its acquisition identifier; the Nmb2 data model carries no such content type, so there is nothing to compare with.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-2, row Object acquisition identifiers

cases.case: User-Agent with product identifier MBSTF and a release version on pull requests
cases.what: Every pull request carries User-Agent "MBSTF/18" followed by the implementation's own product identifier and version, the 18 coming from the fiveg_api_release build option.

cases.case: Server header MBSTF-<host>/<version> on push acknowledgements
cases.what: The push ingest server adds only a Content-Type header to its responses; no Server header is set.

cases.case: Push endpoint exposes HTTP/1.1
cases.what: The push ingest server is a libmicrohttpd daemon, an HTTP/1.1 server.
cases.locator: TS 26.517 V18.6.0 clause 8.2.1.1 (applied to the MBSTF push endpoints by clause 8.2.1.3)

cases.case: Push endpoint supports TLS
cases.what: The push ingest server is started without TLS and its ingest URL is always http://.

noted: Pull requests ask libcurl for HTTP/2; a pulled object without Cache-Control max-age is treated as fresh for 10 s, and a fetch without a deadline times out after 10 s (constants, no clause).
The push server also accepts the non-standard method PUSH alongside PUT and POST.

TS 26.502 V18.6.0 table 4.5.6-2 row Object acquisition method distinguishes retrieving objects once at the start of each active period from checking their validity periodically, but the ObjAcquisitionMethod enumeration of TS 29.581 V18.6.0 clause 6.1.6.3.5 has only PULL and PUSH, so the indication cannot reach the MBSTF. This is a gap at stage 3, not a contradiction, so no verdict is given. SINGLE sessions fetch each object once per entry to ESTABLISHED; manifest sessions revalidate on cache expiry or keepUpdatedInterval.

cases.case: Manifest parsed per the D.1 schema (objects and locator required)
cases.what: The manifest is parsed by the model generated from the object manifest schema, which rejects a document without objects or an object without locator; a manifest that fails to parse is refused.

cases.case: Media type application/3gpp-mbs-object-manifest+json with its version parameter
cases.what: The manifest is accepted with no version parameter or with exactly Rel17; a version parameter holding a comma-separated list, as clause E.3.2 defines it, is refused even when it includes Rel17.

cases.case: updateInterval: manifest re-acquired at that interval with pull acquisition
cases.what: For pull sessions the manifest is scheduled for refetch at its last receipt plus updateInterval seconds.

cases.case: updateInterval ignored with push acquisition
cases.what: The manifest refresh is only scheduled when the session pulls; a pushed manifest's updateInterval is not used.

cases.case: Pulled manifest checked for updates when it gives no updateInterval
cases.what: A pulled object manifest without updateInterval is never fetched again, so changes to it at the origin are not picked up.
cases.locator: TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-2, row Object acquisition method

cases.case: repetitionInterval used for the carousel, MBSTF chooses when omitted
cases.what: Each carousel item takes its repetitionInterval from the manifest, and items without one are given an interval that shares the remaining bit rate.

cases.case: repetitionInterval ignored in Object Collection mode
cases.what: COLLECTION sessions use the list packager, which has no repetition.

cases.case: keepUpdatedInterval: HTTP cache control given precedence (should)
cases.what: The next check is the earlier of the cache expiry and the last fetch plus keepUpdatedInterval, so the manifest value overrides a longer cache lifetime from the origin.

cases.case: keepUpdatedInterval omitted: no checks for updates (shall not)
cases.what: An object without keepUpdatedInterval is fetched again when its cache lifetime ends (10 s when the origin gives none).

cases.case: keepUpdatedInterval ignored in Object Collection mode
cases.what: The same refetch schedule, keepUpdatedInterval included, is applied to COLLECTION sessions.

cases.case: Detected changes reflected at the earliest opportunity
cases.what: A refetched object raises an update event that replaces its entry in the packager queue or carousel.

cases.case: earliestFetchTime: not fetched sooner
cases.what: An object's first fetch is scheduled at the later of now and earliestFetchTime, and it is not treated as active before then.

cases.case: latestFetchTime: not fetched later
cases.what: Objects whose latestFetchTime has passed are skipped when scheduling, and a failed fetch is not retried after it.

cases.case: Manifest pushed by the MBSF at Nmb2
cases.what: A push-based manifest session accepts the manifest at its objAcquisitionIdPush path on the push ingest server and applies each new version pushed there.

requirements.name: FLUTE usage set by the MBSTF

cases.case: Each object handed to FLUTE with an expiry time
cases.what: Every object passed to the FLUTE transmitter is given an expiry time: the list packager takes the cache expiry bounded by the availability start time, the carousel packager the cache expiry, and both fall back to 60 s from now.

cases.case: Content-Location equal to the object distribution URL
cases.what: The Content-Location set on each object is its distribution URL (ingest base URL replaced by the distribution base URL when both are given), updated if it changes between sends.

cases.case: OBJECT_STREAMING: File@Expires no later than the latest availability start time
cases.what: File@Expires is the earlier of the cache expiry and the object's availability start time taken from the MPD.

cases.case: OBJECT_STREAMING: Cache-Control@Expires equal to the availability end time
cases.what: The Cache-Control expiry is set to the object's availability end time when one is known, and left out otherwise.

cases.case: OBJECT_COLLECTION: each FDT Instance describes all objects of the collection (should)
cases.what: The list packager hands the FLUTE transmitter one object at a time and holds the rest in its own queue, so the transmitter, which builds the FDT from the files it holds, knows only the object in transmission.

cases.case: OBJECT_CAROUSEL: the FDT Instance describes all objects currently available (should)
cases.what: The carousel packager hands the transmitter only the items it schedules into its concurrent streams, a number derived from the bit rate, so objects waiting for their next repetition are not among the transmitter's files.

cases.case: OBJECT_STREAMING: FDT describes all objects of the object list not yet fully transmitted (should)
cases.what: As for collections, streaming uses the list packager, which gives the transmitter one object at a time, so objects queued behind it are not described.

noted: The 60 s fallback expiry and the 10 s default cache lifetime that feeds the expiry rest on no clause.
The MBSTF selects the libflute MBS profile and passes Content-Type and ETag for each object; how the FDT is encoded from these is in rt-libflute.

requirements.name: Packet Distribution Method

cases.case: PACKET_PROXY with multicast ingest: join the SSM group given
cases.what: A multicast-ingest session joins the source-specific group from afSsm on the given port; without a source address it joins the group as any-source multicast.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-3, row Packet ingest method

cases.case: Multicast ingest port: destination UDP port or source port
cases.what: The afSsm port number is bound as the local, destination UDP port of the multicast ingest socket.
cases.conflict: TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-3, row MBSTF ingest endpoint addresses: "In the case of Proxy mode, this shall be the Source-Specific Multicast (SSM) endpoint addresses (including the source IP address, destination multicast group address and destination UDP port) nominated by the MBS Application Provider or else by the MBSF." TS 29.581 V18.6.0 clause 6.1.6.2.15, table 6.1.6.2.15-1, row portNumber (ExtSsm): "Source Port"
cases.locator: TS 29.581 V18.6.0 clause 6.1.6.2.15, table 6.1.6.2.15-1, row portNumber

cases.case: Unicast ingest (proxy and forward-only): allocate a listening address and port and return it
cases.what: For unicast ingest a UDP socket is connected to afEgressTunAddr so the system picks the local address and port, and that address is returned in mbStfListenAddr (proxy) or mbStfIngressTunAddr (forward-only).
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-3, row Packet ingest method

cases.case: Unicast ingest: source of incoming packets validated against afEgressTunAddr
cases.what: The ingest socket is connected to afEgressTunAddr and each received datagram's source is compared with it before it is accepted.
cases.locator: TS 29.581 V18.6.0 clause 6.1.6.2.14, table 6.1.6.2.14-1, row afEgressTunAddr

cases.case: PACKET_PROXY: UDP payloads forwarded in new UDP packets
cases.what: Each ingested UDP payload is given a new IP/UDP header with the source and destination address and port from upTrafficFlowInfo before it is sent towards the MB-UPF.

cases.case: PACKET_FORWARD_ONLY: IP packets from the unicast ingest tunnel forwarded without changing their address
cases.what: Forward-only sessions treat each datagram from the ingest tunnel as an encapsulated IP packet and pass it to the MB-UPF tunnel unmodified; a forward-only session that carries upTrafficFlowInfo is refused.
cases.locator: TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-1, row User Plane traffic flow information

cases.case: Multicast ingest refused for forward-only
cases.what: A forward-only session with pktIngestMethod MULTICAST is accepted and joins the afSsm group; nothing restricts multicast ingest to proxy mode.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-3, row Packet ingest method

noted: In proxy mode the new UDP header uses the upTrafficFlowInfo port number as both source and destination port.
The packet scheduling queue size is operator configuration (packetModeSchedulingQueueSize); packets beyond it are discarded.

requirements.name: Transmission towards the MB-UPF (Nmb9)

cases.case: Packets sent through a unicast tunnel to the MB-UPF tunnel endpoint (IPv4 address)
cases.what: Object sessions give the FLUTE transmitter the mbUpfTunAddr IPv4 address and port as its UDP tunnel endpoint; packet sessions send each IP packet as the payload of a UDP datagram to mbUpfTunAddr.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-1, row MBUPF tunnel endpoint address

cases.case: MB-UPF tunnel endpoint given as an IPv6 address, object method
cases.what: Object sessions read only the IPv4 address of mbUpfTunAddr; with an IPv6-only tunnel address the transmitter is given no tunnel and sends the FLUTE packets straight to the multicast group instead.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-1, row MBUPF tunnel endpoint address

cases.case: Destination IP and port, and source address, from upTrafficFlowInfo
cases.what: The FLUTE transmitter (object) and the proxy packetiser (packet) take the multicast destination address, destination port and source address from upTrafficFlowInfo.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-1, row User Plane traffic flow information

cases.case: Transport session identifier from upTrafficFlowInfo
cases.what: The FLUTE transmitter is created with the transportSessionId from upTrafficFlowInfo as its TSI, and an object session without one is refused.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-2, row User Plane traffic flow information

cases.case: Traffic marking (DSCP) applied from dscpMarking
cases.what: dscpMarking is checked for format at creation but never applied to outgoing packets.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-1, row Traffic marking information

cases.case: Scheduling to the target bit rate (mbr)
cases.what: Object sessions pass mbr (in kbit/s) to the FLUTE transmitter as its rate limit and size the carousel against it; packet sessions send through a bit-budget scheduler refilled at mbr.
cases.locator: clause 4.5.6, table 4.5.6-1, row Maximum content bit rate

cases.case: FEC configuration passed through, object method
cases.what: fecInformation is converted to a FLUTE FEC OTI (Compact No-Code means none, Raptor is passed with fecOverHead as the redundancy level); an unsupported scheme stops a SINGLE, COLLECTION or STREAMING session with a packaging failure, and leaves a CAROUSEL session without a transmitter, so no session is sent unprotected.

cases.case: FEC configuration, packet method
cases.what: Packet sessions never read fecInformation; both packet controllers leave FEC unimplemented, so a packet session is sent unprotected whatever FEC it was given.

noted: Packet sessions fall back to 10 kbit/s if mbr were missing, which the mandatory mbr makes unreachable.
The path MTU used for FLUTE packets subtracts a 2-octet GTP_HEADER_SIZE; no clause read here sets that figure.

requirements.name: Content ingest at Nmb8 (Application Provider side)

cases.case: Push-based publishing of objects to the ingest base URL returned by the MBSF
cases.what: The Content Ingest tab lists the objIngUri the MBSF returned for each PUSH Distribution Session, the user appends the object path, and the portal sends the object bytes to that URL.
cases.locator: TS 26.502 V18.6.0 table 4.5.6-2, row Object ingest base URL

cases.case: Ingest parameters taken from the session representation (or the Distribution Session starting event)
cases.what: Push targets are read from objIngUri in the ingest-session representation returned by the MBSF; DIST_SESS_STARTING notifications are shown but not used for this.

cases.case: Push client uses HTTPS when the MBSTF offers it
cases.what: The push client always opens a plain HTTP/1.1 connection whatever the URL scheme and has no HTTPS path; the clause asks clients to prefer HTTPS where it is available.

cases.case: Pull-based origin hosting at Nmb8
cases.what: Two origins exist: the portal serves files under /content without its login, and rt-mbs-examples' express-mock-media-server serves its public directory; the demo scripts point objIngUri at the mock server, not at the portal.

cases.case: Object ingest base URL for PULL nominated by the Application Provider
cases.what: For PULL sessions the form and the demo scripts send objIngUri set to the origin's base URL.
cases.locator: TS 26.502 V18.6.0 table 4.5.6-2, row Object ingest base URL

cases.case: Object manifests served with the registered media type and version parameter
cases.what: The portal labels every .json file under /content, and the mock server labels its carousel and collection manifest files, as application/3gpp-mbs-object-manifest+json;version="Rel17".

cases.case: Packet ingest towards the MBSTF ingest endpoint
cases.what: Neither the portal nor rt-mbs-examples sends a packet stream to the ingest endpoint provisioned for a PACKET session; the portal only provisions PACKET sessions and shows the returned addresses, and the one packet sender in rt-mbs-examples streams to a fixed multicast group, not to a provisioned endpoint.

noted: Objects are pushed with HTTP PUT. Only the informative Annex B of TS 26.502 V18.6.0 (figure B.2.2-1, 'HTTP PUT') shows a method; no normative clause read fixes it.

Both pull origins answer over cleartext HTTP/1.1 only. TS 26.517 V18.6.0 clause 8.2.1.1 asks for TLS on 'content interfaces at reference points specified in the present document'; whether the Application Provider's pull origin at Nmb8 is one of them is not stated in the clauses read.

Both origins send ETag and Last-Modified and honour conditional requests; the portal sets max-age=30 on everything, the mock server sets no-cache on MPDs. The ETag/Last-Modified obligations in TS 26.517 V18.6.0 clause 8.2.1.4 are addressed to the MBS AF, not to the Application Provider.

TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 5.3 step 11 has the Distribution Session starting event carry the chosen ingest parameters, but EventNotification in TS 29.580 V18.8.0 table 6.2.6.2.10-1 has no attribute for them other than the free-text statusAddInfo.

The docker compose setup in rt-mbs-examples (mbs-docker-setup) runs the core, MBSF, MBSTF and RAN images but neither the portal, the dashboard nor the mock media server; the mock server has its own compose file on port 3004. The portal, dashboard and mock server run only through the bash demo scripts.
The mock server requires the etag module but does not declare it in its package.json; it resolves only through express's own dependency.

features.name: MBS User Service Announcement
features.summary: The MBSF writes User Service Descriptions, Session Description documents and multipart bundles, serves the MBS-5 retrieval API with entity tags and conditional requests, and runs the announcement channel by pushing an object manifest; the bundle on the channel carries a single description where a descriptions document is required, there is no document version, main language, radio parameters, security description or cancelled schedule, the MBS AF has no TLS or Cache-Control and a non-conformant Server header, the bundle URL for MBS-1 reaches the Application Provider only with the announcement channel, and the specifications disagree on the repair locator and the empty discovery result.

cases.case: Document is UserServiceDescriptions (version, userServiceDescriptions array) at MBS-5
cases.what: The MBS-5 discovery and retrieval responses carry a UserServiceDescriptions document listing one User Service Description per matching service.

cases.case: Document is UserServiceDescriptions in the bundle carried on the announcement channel and at the private bundle URL
cases.what: The root of the per-session bundle is a single User Service Description object, not a UserServiceDescriptions document, although it is labelled with the UserServiceDescriptions media type.

cases.case: version of the User Service Descriptions document
cases.what: No version number is written, so every delivered document replaces the previous one.

cases.case: serviceIds from the external service identifiers
cases.what: Copies extServiceIds of the MBS User Service into serviceIds.

cases.case: class from servClass
cases.what: Copies servClass into class.

cases.case: names and descriptions per language
cases.what: Writes one name and one description entry per ServiceNameDescription that carries them, each with its language.

cases.case: serviceLanguage from mainServLang
cases.what: mainServLang is not passed to the announcement, so serviceLanguage is never written.
cases.locator: TS 26.502 V18.6.0 clause 4.5.7, table 4.5.7-1, row Main service language

cases.case: distributionSessionDescriptions: one per MBS Distribution Session
cases.what: Adds one Distribution Session Description for each MBS Distribution Session of the ingest session.

cases.case: serviceScheduleDescriptions from the active periods
cases.what: Writes one Service Schedule Description per active period, or one with a repetition rule, and none when no period is provisioned.

cases.case: Media type with profiles and version="Rel18"
cases.what: Labels the document application/3gpp-mbs-user-service-descriptions+json with profiles="urn:3GPP:26517:17:baseline" and version="Rel18".

requirements.name: Distribution Session Description

cases.case: distributionMethod
cases.what: Copies distrMethod (OBJECT or PACKET).

cases.case: conformanceProfiles (omitted for the Baseline profile)
cases.what: Never writes conformanceProfiles, which clause 12.3 allows for sessions conforming to the Baseline profile.

cases.case: sessionDescriptionLocator is an absolute URL
cases.what: Writes a relative locator, the Distribution Session key with ".sdp", resolved against the bundle; the table types it AbsoluteUrl while the schema types it Uri, and an absolute URL would satisfy both.
cases.locator: clause 5.2.4, table 5.2.4-1, row sessionDescriptionLocator (data type AbsoluteUrl)

cases.case: applicationServiceDescriptions: entryPointLocator and contentType
cases.what: Writes one entry per object acquisition identifier under the distribution (or ingest) base URL, with a content type taken from the file extension through the system MIME table.

cases.case: postSessionObjectRepairParameters (back-off, distribution base, repair base)
cases.what: Writes back-off parameters, objectDistributionBaseLocator and a repair base under the configured MBS AS URL when object repair is configured, and withholds them for OBJECT_STREAMING.

cases.case: Object repair base: objectRepairBaseLocators (array, table) or objectRepairBaseLocator (single, schema)
cases.what: Writes a single objectRepairBaseLocator, the form the Annex A.2.1 schema defines.
cases.conflict: TS 26.517 V18.6.0 clause 5.2.8, table 5.2.8-1 defines the property "object‌Repair‌BaseLocators" of type "array(AbsoluteUrl)"; Annex A.2.1 (TS26517_MBSUserServiceAnnouncement.yaml, ObjectRepairParameters) defines "objectRepairBaseLocator" with a single AbsoluteUrl.
