features.name: MB-SMF service consumer (MBSF side)
features.summary: The MB-SMF client library creates, updates and releases MBS sessions and creates and deletes status subscriptions with the request shapes TS 29.532 defines, and reads the 201 response in full; a subscription update sends the session changes instead of the subscription changes, notifications are answered 200 rather than 204, the associated session ID is never sent, and the MBSF never subscribes to status notifications.

requirements.name: MB-SMF client: Nmbsmf_MBSSession requests

cases.case: Create (POST /mbs-sessions)
cases.what: Sends CreateReqData with the MBS Session ID or tmgiAllocReq, service type, location dependence, ingress tunnel request, service areas, DNN, S-NSSAI, times, MBS service information, activity status, anyUeInd and FSA IDs, and the first status subscription when one is set.

cases.case: Read the 201 response
cases.what: Takes the session reference from Location, and the TMGI and expiration time, ingress tunnel, SSM, redMbsServArea and any event reports from the body; a missing TMGI or tunnel that was asked for fails the creation.

cases.case: Update (PATCH /mbs-sessions/{mbsSessionRef})
cases.what: Sends the changes since the last accepted state as a JSON Patch, and on 200 or 204 keeps the new state and any redMbsServArea, or on an error restores the previous state and reports the ProblemDetails.

cases.case: Release (DELETE /mbs-sessions/{mbsSessionRef})
cases.what: Sends DELETE on the stored session reference.

cases.case: StatusSubscribe: create (POST /mbs-sessions/subscriptions)
cases.what: Sends the MBS Session ID, Area Session ID, events, notification URI, correlation ID, expiry time and its NF instance ID, and opens a notification server.

cases.case: StatusSubscribe: read the 201 response
cases.what: The response handler is given a message whose HTTP headers were not parsed, so the subscription identifier in the Location header of a 201 response is not obtained.

cases.case: StatusSubscribe: update (PATCH /mbs-sessions/subscriptions/{subscriptionId})
cases.what: Sends the pending changes of the MBS session as the patch body, not changes to the subscription, and does not read the response.

cases.case: StatusUnsubscribe (DELETE /mbs-sessions/subscriptions/{subscriptionId})
cases.what: Sends DELETE on the subscription identifier.

cases.case: StatusNotify received: event reports passed to the application
cases.what: Parses StatusNotifyReqData on the notification server, finds the subscription by URI and passes each TMGI expiry, broadcast delivery status and ingress tunnel event to the application.

cases.case: StatusNotify answered 204 No Content
cases.what: Answers 200 OK; the OpenAPI callback defines 204 No Content as the only success response.
cases.locator: clause 5.3.2.8.1 step 2a; TS29532_Nmbsmf_MBSSession.yaml, callback statusNotification, responses

cases.case: Associated Session ID and NR RedCap UE information in Create
cases.what: The associated session ID the caller sets is held but never sent, because the request model has no such attribute, and there is no NR RedCap field.

noted: The deletion callback is raised for any answer to a Release, an error included.
No expiry time is sent for a subscription carried inside the Create request.
The Create builder serialises the body itself because the SBI library has no CreateReqData encoder.

requirements.name: MBSF use of Nmbsmf_MBSSession

cases.case: Ingress transport address requested when an MBSTF is used
cases.what: Every MBS session the MBSF creates for a distribution session requests an ingress tunnel, and the returned tunnel is checked.

cases.case: TMGI allocation requested in the Create
cases.what: Requests a TMGI when the distribution session has no MBS Session ID, or has an SSM with locationDependent true, and passes on a TMGI the AF supplied otherwise.

cases.case: Service type taken from the MBS User Service
cases.what: Sends BROADCAST or MULTICAST according to the service type of the parent MBS User Service.

cases.case: Release when the distribution session is removed
cases.what: Deletes the subscription, if any, and the MBS session once per object.

cases.case: Delivery status subscription for a legacy AS
cases.what: The MBSF never creates a status subscription at the MB-SMF.

noted: The MBSF never calls Nmbsmf_TMGI; it obtains TMGIs only through MBS session creation.

features.name: NGAP broadcast session management at the gNB
features.summary: The gNB-CU-CP answers Broadcast Session Setup, Modification and Release from the AMF, drives the E1AP and F1AP procedures behind each, and returns its own N3mb endpoint; it does not use the MBS service area or the MBS FSA IDs to choose cells, does not act on the Release 18 Supported UE Type List or Associated Session ID, does not answer a Release for an unknown session, never initiates Broadcast Session Release Required, and has the Release 18 Broadcast Session Transport procedure coded but never started.

requirements.name: Broadcast Session Setup

cases.case: BROADCAST SESSION SETUP REQUEST handled
cases.what: The NGAP layer dispatches the request, decodes the MBS Session ID, S-NSSAI, MBS service area and the MBS Session Setup Request Transfer, creates a CU-CP MBS session and starts the setup routine on the MBS task scheduler.

cases.case: BROADCAST SESSION SETUP RESPONSE after resources are set up
cases.what: The Response is sent only after the E1AP BC Bearer Context Setup, the F1AP Broadcast Context Setup and the follow-up E1AP BC Bearer Context Modification all succeed, with one MRB per MBS QoS flow.

cases.case: MBS Session Setup Response Transfer: MBS Session TNL Information NG-RAN
cases.what: The Response carries the transfer IE with the CU-UP N3mb endpoint (bind address and local TEID) as location-independent Shared NG-U Unicast TNL Information; location-dependent sessions get no transfer IE.

cases.case: MBS Service Area taken into account
cases.what: The service area is decoded and copied into the F1AP Broadcast Context Setup Request, but no part of the gNB uses it to choose cells: the DU serves the first of its own cells named in the CU-to-DU cell list; the clause requires the area to be taken into account as TS 23.247 specifies.

cases.case: MBS Session FSA ID List taken into account
cases.what: The FSA ID list is decoded into the request and then not read anywhere; cells and frequencies are not chosen from it.

cases.case: BROADCAST SESSION SETUP FAILURE when no resources can be provided
cases.what: A decode error, a duplicate MBS Session ID, a failed CU-CP session creation, or a failure of any E1AP or F1AP step answers with BROADCAST SESSION SETUP FAILURE carrying a cause (the E1AP or F1AP cause category mapped to NGAP, value unspecified) and an MBS Session Setup Failure Transfer.

cases.case: Supported UE Type List taken into account (Release 18, if supported)
cases.what: The codec decodes the IE inside the MBS Session Setup or Modification Request Transfer, but nothing outside the codec reads it, so MBS session resources are configured the same way whatever UE types the 5GC names.

cases.case: Associated Session ID used to decide MBS session resource sharing (Release 18, if supported)
cases.what: The codec decodes the IE in the request, but the conversion to the CU-CP request does not copy it and nothing decides whether sessions from different 5GCs can share resources.

noted: Each MBS QoS flow gets its own MRB; several flows are never mapped to one MRB.
When a later step fails, the E1AP and F1AP contexts already set up for the session are not released by the setup routine.

cases.case: Replace the QoS flow list (add, update, remove MRBs)
cases.what: Flows recorded for the session but absent from the new list are removed, unmapped flows get new MRBs and mapped flows get their QoS updated, through E1AP BC Bearer Context Modification, then F1AP Broadcast Context Modification, then an E1AP sync of the new F1-U endpoints, after which the Response is sent.

cases.case: Update the MBS service area
cases.what: A new MBS service area is forwarded to the DU in the F1AP Broadcast Context Modification Request, but the DU does not read it, so the area served does not change.

cases.case: BROADCAST SESSION MODIFICATION FAILURE
cases.what: A decode error, an unknown session, or a failure of any E1AP or F1AP step answers with BROADCAST SESSION MODIFICATION FAILURE and a cause.

cases.case: Supported UE Type List taken into account on Modification (Release 18, if supported)
cases.what: The codec decodes the IE inside the MBS Session Setup or Modification Request Transfer, but nothing outside the codec reads it.

cases.case: Stop broadcasting and release all session resources
cases.what: The release routine sends F1AP Broadcast Context Release Command, then E1AP BC Bearer Context Release Command, then removes the CU-CP session, before the Response.

cases.case: BROADCAST SESSION RELEASE RESPONSE for a known session
cases.what: Sends the Response with the MBS Session ID once the routine finishes.

cases.case: BROADCAST SESSION RELEASE RESPONSE for an unknown session
cases.what: A Release Request for a session the gNB has no context for is logged and dropped with no Response; the clause requires a Response on reception of the message.

cases.case: Send BROADCAST SESSION RELEASE REQUIRED
cases.what: No code builds or sends the message; the generated codec type is never used.

requirements.name: Broadcast Session Transport (Release 18)

cases.case: Send BROADCAST SESSION TRANSPORT REQUEST
cases.what: A procedure that sends the request and waits for the Response or Failure exists in the NGAP layer, but nothing in the CU-CP calls it, so the request is never sent.

requirements.exists: The NGAP codec carries the Release 18 messages and an NGAP procedure that sends the request and handles the Response and Failure.

features.name: MB-UPF to gNB user plane (N3mb, shared delivery)
features.summary: The gNB-CU-UP joins the IP multicast group the 5G Core signals for the session, terminates the shared GTP-U tunnel and passes packets through SDAP and an unciphered PDCP entity per MRB towards the DU; it registers the tunnel under the byte-reversed TEID rather than the signalled one, and the 5GC unicast transport option is not offered.

requirements.name: Shared NG-U multicast transport

cases.case: IP Multicast Address: join the group
cases.what: The CU-UP takes the IP multicast address from the BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at 5GC (location-independent, or the entry matching the area session) and joins it on its NG-U gateway; a failed join fails the setup.

cases.case: GTP-TEID at 5GC: identify the tunnel
cases.what: The CU-UP registers the tunnel under the signalled TEID with its four bytes reversed; its code comment says this matches the byte order the MB-UPF of the 5G Core used here puts on the wire (not checked in this part). A 5G Core that sends the TEID it signalled would not match the tunnel.

cases.case: IP Source Address
cases.what: The address is decoded and carried to the CU-UP; reception joins the group without a source filter.

noted: If the 5G Core omits MBS Session TNL Information 5GC, the CU-UP cannot resolve a tunnel identifier and the whole Broadcast Session Setup fails.

requirements.name: PDCP for broadcast MRBs at the gNB-CU-UP

cases.case: No ciphering or integrity protection
cases.what: Each MRB PDCP entity is configured with integrity and ciphering both off.

cases.case: pdcp-SN-SizeDL 18 and t-Reordering ms0 (TS 38.331 clause 9.1.1.7)
cases.what: The CU-CP requests an 18-bit DL SN and t-Reordering ms0 for every MRB, and the PDCP configuration it sends in MRB-PDCP-ConfigBroadcast-r17 leaves both fields absent so the same defaults apply at the UE.

features.name: F1AP broadcast context (gNB-CU and gNB-DU)
features.summary: Broadcast Context Setup, Modification and Release run between the CU-CP and the DU, with MRB setup, modify and release and both failure messages; the DU does not answer some setup failures, never reports MRBs that failed in a Modification, ignores the MBS service area and never reports the Release 18 Broadcast Area Scope, the CU does not act on MRBs the DU reports as failed, and Broadcast Context Release Request and the Release 18 Broadcast Transport Resource Request are not sent or handled.

requirements.name: Broadcast Context Setup

cases.case: BROADCAST CONTEXT SETUP REQUEST sent by the gNB-CU
cases.what: The CU-CP sends the request with MBS Session ID, MBS service area, S-NSSAI, the CU-to-DU RRC information (cell list, per-MRB PDCP configuration) and one Broadcast MRB per E1AP-confirmed MRB with its F1-U endpoint at the CU.

cases.case: Broadcast MRB Setup List in the Response
cases.what: The DU creates the session in its cell, sets up each MRB and lists those set up, with their F1-U endpoint at the DU.

cases.case: Broadcast MRB Failed To Be Setup List in the Response
cases.what: MRBs the DU could not set up are listed in the Failed To Be Setup List when others succeed.

cases.case: gNB-CU regards the MRBs failed to be setup
cases.what: The CU-CP ignores the Failed To Be Setup List: it only leaves those MRBs out of the follow-up E1AP modification, so their CU-UP resources and QoS-flow mapping remain and the AMF is not told.

cases.case: MBS Service Area used for shared F1-U tunnel assignment
cases.what: The DU does not read the MBS Service Area IE of the request.

cases.case: BROADCAST CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE
cases.what: The DU sends the Failure when MRB configuration fails after the session was created, but when none of its cells matches the request, when the session cannot be created, when no session index is free, or when the CU ID is already in use, it logs and sends nothing.

cases.case: Broadcast Area Scope in the Response (Release 18)
cases.what: The codec carries the IE, but the DU never includes it in BROADCAST CONTEXT SETUP RESPONSE, so the CU is not told in which cells the session resources were set up; the CU-CP includes the MBS Service Area IE whenever the AMF provided one, so the condition arises.

cases.case: Supported UE Type List stored and used (Release 18, if supported)
cases.what: The codec carries the IE in the request; the CU-CP never sets it and the DU never reads it.

cases.case: Associated Session ID used to decide MBS session resource sharing (Release 18, if supported)
cases.what: The codec carries the IE in the request; the CU-CP never sets it and the DU never reads it.

noted: One cell per broadcast context: the DU serves the first cell of the CU-to-DU cell list that it owns.

requirements.name: Broadcast Context Modification

cases.case: Broadcast MRB To Be Setup List: set up and list in Broadcast MRB Setup List
cases.what: New MRBs are set up and listed with their DU F1-U endpoint; MCCH is rebuilt.

cases.case: Broadcast MRB Failed To Be Setup List
cases.what: MRBs the DU rejects are recorded by the DU manager but never copied into the F1AP response, so the list is never sent.

cases.case: Broadcast MRB To Be Modified List: update and list in Broadcast MRB Modified List
cases.what: Each MRB to modify is torn down and recreated from the updated configuration under the same MRB ID, and listed as modified.

cases.case: Broadcast MRB Failed To Be Modified List
cases.what: MRBs that fail to be modified are recorded in the DU resource response but not passed to the F1AP response, so the list is never sent.

cases.case: Broadcast MRB To Be Released List
cases.what: Listed MRBs are torn down and their LCIDs freed; MCCH is rebuilt.

cases.case: BROADCAST CONTEXT MODIFICATION FAILURE
cases.what: When the DU resource update or the MAC reconfiguration fails, the DU answers with the Failure and cause radio network "no radio resources available".

cases.case: BROADCAST CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUEST sent by the gNB-CU
cases.what: The CU-CP sends the request from NGAP Broadcast Session Modification and from E1AP BC Bearer Context Modification Required, and waits for the Response or Failure.

cases.case: MBS Service Area in the Modification Request: release, establish and replace cells (Release 18)
cases.what: The CU-CP forwards a new MBS Service Area, but the DU does not read it, so no cell is released or added and the stored area is not replaced.

cases.case: Broadcast Area Scope in the Modification Response (Release 18)
cases.what: The codec carries the IE, but the DU never includes it in BROADCAST CONTEXT MODIFICATION RESPONSE.

cases.case: Supported UE Type List stored and used on Modification (Release 18, if supported)
cases.what: The codec carries the IE in the request; the CU-CP never sets it and the DU never reads it.

noted: A Modification Request with an unknown gNB-DU MBS F1AP ID is discarded without a reply.

cases.case: Release resources and reply BROADCAST CONTEXT RELEASE COMPLETE
cases.what: The DU runs its MBS session deletion (F1AP context, MAC and scheduler resources, MCCH rebuild) and then sends Release Complete with both F1AP IDs.

requirements.name: Broadcast Context Release Request

cases.case: gNB-DU sends BROADCAST CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST
cases.what: The DU builds the message but the send call is commented out and the cause is not set, so the message is never sent.

cases.case: gNB-CU triggers Broadcast Context Release on reception
cases.what: The CU-CP F1AP layer has no case for the message.

requirements.exists: A DU function that fills the message IDs exists.

requirements.name: Broadcast Transport Resource Request (Release 18)

cases.case: BROADCAST TRANSPORT RESOURCE REQUEST sent by the gNB-DU
cases.what: The F1AP codec carries the message, but no DU code builds or sends it.

cases.case: gNB-CU triggers Broadcast Context Modification on reception
cases.what: No CU-CP code handles the message.

requirements.exists: The F1AP codec carries the Release 18 message, including the F1-U Path Failure indication.

features.name: E1AP broadcast bearer context (gNB-CU-CP and gNB-CU-UP)
features.summary: BC Bearer Context Setup, Modification and Release work between CU-CP and CU-UP with per-MRB and per-flow result lists and F1-U endpoints, and the CU-CP reacts to Modification Required and Release Request; both Failure messages leave the Cause unset, a changed 5GC NG-U address is not applied, and the shared NG-U termination options are not acted on.

cases.case: BC MRB Setup Response List and BC MRB Failed List
cases.what: Each requested MRB is reported as set up or failed with a cause (for example an unsupported 5QI).

cases.case: MBS QoS Flow Setup List and MBS QoS Flow Failed List per MRB
cases.what: Each flow is mapped in SDAP and reported as set up, or as failed with cause "multiple QoS flow ID instances" or "not supported 5QI".

cases.case: F1-U TNL Info Added List
cases.what: For each requested F1-U context reference the CU-UP allocates an F1-U endpoint and returns it in the F1-U TNL Info Added List.

cases.case: Requested Action for Available Shared NG-U Termination
cases.what: The CU-CP always sends "apply requested configuration" and the CU-UP decodes the value but does not act on it or report an Available BC MRB Configuration.

cases.case: BC BEARER CONTEXT SETUP FAILURE with a cause
cases.what: The Failure is sent when session resources cannot be set up, but the cause the CU-UP computed is not copied into it: only the gNB-CU-CP MBS E1AP ID is filled.

cases.case: Response on partial success, with BC MRB Setup or Modify Response List and BC MRB Failed List
cases.what: MRBs to set up, modify and remove are applied; success of any item gives a Response listing set-up or modified MRBs, their flow results and failed MRBs with causes.

cases.case: F1-U TNL Info at DU added or modified for an MRB
cases.what: The DU F1-U endpoint carried in the modification is applied to the MRB F1-U bearer; this is how the CU-CP completes setup after F1AP.

cases.case: BC Bearer Context NG-U TNL Info at 5GC To Setup or Modify
cases.what: The CU-UP modification handler applies only the MRB lists; a new 5GC NG-U address is ignored.

cases.case: BC BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION FAILURE with a cause
cases.what: The Failure is sent when no requested item succeeds, but its Cause is not filled.

requirements.name: BC Bearer Context Modification Required (gNB-CU-UP initiated)

cases.case: gNB-CU-CP replies BC BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION CONFIRM
cases.what: The CU-CP releases the listed MRBs at the DU through F1AP Broadcast Context Modification and then sends the Confirm.

cases.case: gNB-CU-UP sends BC BEARER CONTEXT MODIFICATION REQUIRED
cases.what: The CU-UP E1AP layer has a sender that waits for the Confirm, but nothing in the CU-UP calls it, so the message is never sent.

cases.case: Release resources and reply BC BEARER CONTEXT RELEASE COMPLETE
cases.what: The CU-UP releases the GTP-U tunnel, SDAP and PDCP entities and F1-U bearers of the session, then sends Release Complete with both E1AP IDs.

requirements.name: BC Bearer Context Release Request (gNB-CU-UP initiated)

cases.case: gNB-CU-CP initiates BC Bearer Context Release
cases.what: The CU-CP schedules the BC Bearer Context Release Command for the session; F1AP and NGAP state are left as they are.

cases.case: gNB-CU-UP sends BC BEARER CONTEXT RELEASE REQUEST
cases.what: The CU-UP E1AP layer has a sender for the message, but nothing in the CU-UP calls it, so the message is never sent.

features.name: MCCH and SIB20 broadcast signalling at the gNB
features.summary: The DU advertises SIB20 and SIB21 in SIB1, broadcasts SIB20 from operator settings, sends MCCH on PDCCH addressed to MCCH-RNTI with DCI format 4_0 inside the configured window, changes MCCH only at modification-period boundaries and signals the change, with no Release 18 (e)RedCap CFR; it sends MCCH every radio frame whatever repetition period SIB20 advertises, can flag a new service as an "other modification", and sends MCCH as a bare RRC message without the MAC subheader and RLC header the logical channel requires.

requirements.name: SIB1 scheduling information and SIB20 content

cases.case: SIB20 and SIB21 listed in SIB1 (SchedulingInfo2-r17, SIB-TypeInfo-v1700)
cases.what: SIB20 and SIB21 entries of an SI message are encoded as type1-r17 entries of schedulingInfoList2-r17 in SIB1 and the SI message is sent on the SI-RNTI scheduler.

cases.case: mcch-Config-r17 (repetition period and offset, window start slot, window duration, modification period)
cases.what: All four fields come from operator options and are packed into SIB20; window duration has no value 1, and the rf1 arm carries 0.

cases.case: cfr-ConfigMCCH-MTCH-r17
cases.what: The field is never sent, so the UE uses CORESET#0 and the initial BWP PDSCH configuration, which is what the DU schedules MCCH and MTCH in.

cases.case: searchSpaceMCCH-r17 and searchSpaceMTCH-r17 in PDCCH-ConfigCommon
cases.what: Both are set in the PDCCH-ConfigCommon of SIB1, to the search spaces the scheduler uses for MCCH and MTCH.

cases.case: CFR and MCCH configuration for (e)RedCap UEs in SIB20 (Release 18)
cases.what: The RRC codec carries the SIB20 Release 18 extension (cfr-ConfigMCCH-MTCH-RedCap, mcch-ConfigRedCap), but the DU never fills it, so no separate RedCap CFR is configured.

noted: Operator options for the CFR location and bandwidth are parsed but not copied into SIB20.
searchSpaceMCCH-r17 and searchSpaceMTCH-r17 are set even when MBS is not configured.
A repetition offset larger than the period is clamped to period - 1 without a warning.

requirements.name: MCCH scheduling

cases.case: PDCCH addressed to MCCH-RNTI (0xFFFD)
cases.what: MCCH PDCCH is allocated in the common search space with MCCH-RNTI 0xFFFD.

cases.case: Transmission window from mcch-WindowStartSlot for mcch-WindowDuration
cases.what: The window opens at the configured start slot and lasts the configured duration, one slot when the duration is absent; MCCH is sent once in the first usable slot of the window.

cases.case: Repetition period and offset
cases.what: The window recurs every radio frame; SFN, repetition period and offset are not used, so the schedule disagrees with SIB20 whenever the operator sets a period other than one frame.

noted: MCCH uses TDRA row 0, MCS 5, aggregation level 4 and RV 0, fixed in code.
A window start slot beyond the slots of one frame at the cell numerology is logged and MCCH is then never sent.

requirements.name: MCCH modification period and change notification

cases.case: Change only at a modification-period boundary
cases.what: A new MCCH is staged and swapped in at the slot where SFN mod period is 0 at the window start slot; the first MCCH of a cell starts at once.

cases.case: Notification from the start of that period, in every repetition
cases.what: Notification starts at the same boundary and is set on each MCCH sent until a count of one modification period of transmissions is used up.

cases.case: MSB set for the start of a new MBS service
cases.what: A new session is announced with the MSB only if its MRBs are already known when it is created; when they arrive in the following configuration step, that update replaces the pending one and the session is announced with the LSB.

cases.case: LSB set for other modifications (configuration change, session stop)
cases.what: MRB changes and session deletion set the LSB.

cases.case: Field layout (FDRA on CORESET#0 size, TDRA 4, VRB-to-PRB 1, MCS 5, RV 2, notification 2, reserved 14)
cases.what: One packer builds format 4_0 for both MCCH-RNTI and G-RNTI with these widths.

cases.case: MCCH change notification only with MCCH-RNTI, reserved otherwise
cases.what: The 2-bit field is always present; G-RNTI DCIs carry 0 in it.

cases.case: MAC subPDU with LCID 0 (Table 6.2.1-1c)
cases.what: The MCCH transport block is the RRC message followed by zero padding, with no MAC subheader; a transparent MAC PDU is defined only for PCH, BCH and BCCH.

cases.case: RLC UM on MCCH (TS 38.331 clause 9.1.1.6: UM, sn-FieldLength 6)
cases.what: No RLC entity carries MCCH, so the message has no UMD header.

requirements.name: MBSBroadcastConfiguration content

cases.case: mbs-SessionId (TMGI)
cases.what: The TMGI is built from the cell PLMN and the first three octets of the six-octet TMGI value received over F1AP, not from the TMGI the 5G Core assigned (whose PLMN may differ).

cases.case: g-RNTI
cases.what: Each session carries the G-RNTI the MAC allocated for it.

cases.case: mrb-ListBroadcast (PDCP and RLC configuration, logicalChannelIdentity)
cases.what: One entry per MRB with its LCID; PDCP SN size, t-Reordering, RLC SN length and t-Reassembly are left absent so the TS 38.331 clause 9.1.1.7 values apply, matching the 18-bit PDCP and 12-bit RLC the gNB uses.

cases.case: Every MRB of a session listed
cases.what: At most four MRBs per session are listed; further MRBs are carried on MTCH but left out of MCCH.

noted: mtch-SchedulingInfo, pdsch-ConfigIndex, mtch-NeighbourCell, drx-ConfigPTM-List, pdsch-ConfigMTCH and mbs-NeighbourCellList are never sent (all optional).
Session creation and deletion rebuild MCCH without filtering out multicast sessions, which the configuration step does filter.

cases.case: mbs-FSAI-IntraFreq-r17
cases.what: Filled from operator-configured FSAIs and packed as 3-octet values.

cases.case: mbs-FSAI-InterFreqList-r17
cases.what: No configuration fills the inter-frequency list, so it is never sent (a single-cell scope stated in the code).

features.name: MRB and MTCH scheduling at the gNB
features.summary: Each broadcast session gets a G-RNTI and its MRBs get LCIDs; MTCH is scheduled with DCI format 4_0 scrambled by the G-RNTI, without HARQ feedback, over RLC UM; G-RNTIs are taken from the C-RNTI range without checking for UEs, and a statically configured MRB on an LCID below 21 is advertised but never scheduled.

requirements.name: G-RNTI and MTCH logical channel identities

cases.case: One G-RNTI per broadcast session
cases.what: The MAC allocates a G-RNTI per session from its own counter starting at 0x5501, unique among MBS sessions.

cases.case: MTCH LCIDs in 1 to 32
cases.what: Dynamic MRBs get LCIDs 21 to 32, unique across the DU.

cases.case: Statically configured MRB scheduled on its advertised LCID
cases.what: A statically configured session is advertised on MCCH with its MRB and LCID (default 1, any of 1 to 32), but it never enters the DU session database, so no MRB, RLC entity or scheduler session is created for it and no MTCH is sent for it; the MTCH scheduler would in any case serve only LCIDs 21 to 32.

noted: G-RNTIs come from the C-RNTI value range and are not checked against UE C-RNTIs; a static G-RNTI is not range-checked at all.
LCIDs are allocated across the whole DU, not per G-RNTI, because the UE keys MRBs by LCID alone; this caps concurrent MRBs at twelve.

requirements.name: MTCH transmission

cases.case: PDCCH DCI format 4_0 with CRC scrambled by G-RNTI in searchSpaceMTCH
cases.what: MTCH grants use format 4_0 with the session G-RNTI in the search space signalled as searchSpaceMTCH.

cases.case: No HARQ feedback, new data each grant
cases.what: No PUCCH resource is reserved and every MTCH transport block is new data with no retransmission.

cases.case: RLC UM, 12-bit SN, DL only (TS 38.331 clause 9.1.1.7)
cases.what: MRB RLC entities are unidirectional DL UM with 12-bit SN.

noted: MCS is fixed (index 10 by default, changeable by option or remote command); the dynamic MCS path has an unchecked access when no MCS fits.
One MBS PDSCH per slot; slots covered by the MCCH window are skipped and the top four CRBs are kept free for MCCH.

requirements.name: Broadcast DRX (PTM DRX)

cases.case: drx-ConfigPTM-List and mtch-SchedulingInfo
cases.what: No PTM DRX configuration is built or applied; the scheduler placeholder for it is always empty. The configuration is optional for the network.

requirements.exists: A placeholder field for a PTM DRX configuration in the scheduler session request.

features.name: UE broadcast reception
features.summary: The UE reads SIB20, decodes MCCH on MCCH-RNTI inside the window, joins every advertised session, decodes MTCH on the G-RNTIs and delivers packets through RLC UM and PDCP with the correct start-of-reception rules; it ignores the repetition period and the change notification, never re-reads SIB20, expects MCCH without MAC and RLC headers, applies its own defaults instead of the specified ones when PDCP t-Reordering and RLC t-Reassembly are absent, has no SDAP, broadcast DRX or MBS Interest Indication, and keys MRBs by LCID alone.

cases.case: SIB20 decoded from the SI message
cases.what: SIB20 and SIB21 are taken from SystemInformation and SIB20 is stored whole.

cases.case: SI message located from SIB1 schedulingInfoList2-r17
cases.what: SIB1 scheduling information for SIB20 is not read; SI-RNTI search is left on after SIB1 until SIB20 has been seen.

cases.case: SIB20 re-read on a new cell or a change
cases.what: Only the first SIB20 is processed; the flag is never cleared, so a later or different SIB20 is ignored.

cases.case: Start MCCH acquisition upon SIB20
cases.what: MCCH search starts as soon as SIB20 is stored.

cases.case: PDCCH addressed to MCCH-RNTI (0xFFFD) in the MCCH window
cases.what: MCCH-RNTI is searched inside a window opened at mcch-WindowStartSlot for mcch-WindowDuration slots.

cases.case: Window when mcch-WindowDuration is absent
cases.what: The UE assumes a two-slot window; absence means MCCH is only in the start slot.

cases.case: Window start slot beyond the first ten slots
cases.what: The window position is computed on ten slots per frame, so start slots 10 to 79 (valid at higher numerologies) never open a window.

cases.case: Repetition period and offset
cases.what: Not read; the UE expects a window every radio frame.

cases.case: Acquire on change notification (MSB new service, LSB other change)
cases.what: The 2-bit field is unpacked from DCI format 4_0 but never read; the UE instead re-reads MCCH about every 100 slots.

cases.case: MCCH information overwrites stored information
cases.what: Each decoded MCCH adds new sessions and releases missing ones, but an LCID already set up is skipped, so a changed configuration of an existing MRB is never applied.

cases.case: MCCH carried as a MAC subPDU on LCID 0 over RLC UM
cases.what: The UE decodes the transport block directly as an MCCH-Message with no MAC subheader and no RLC entity, mirroring the gNB; a standard MCCH would not decode.

cases.case: searchSpaceMCCH
cases.what: searchSpaceMCCH is not decoded; format 4_0 is searched in Type0 CSS / search space 0 and any other search space listing it.

cases.case: Field layout with FDRA on CORESET#0 size
cases.what: All fields are unpacked with the specified widths; the notification bits are zeroed unless the RNTI is MCCH-RNTI.

requirements.name: Broadcast MRB establishment

cases.case: PDCP entity: SN size (12 if signalled, else 18)
cases.what: PDCP is created per MRB with a 12-bit SN when pdcp-SN-SizeDL is present and 18 bits otherwise.

cases.case: PDCP t-Reordering when absent (ms0)
cases.what: The UE applies 500 ms when the field is absent.

cases.case: RLC UM entity: SN length (6 if signalled, else 12)
cases.what: RLC UM is created per MRB with the signalled or default SN length.

cases.case: RLC t-Reassembly when absent (ms0)
cases.what: The UE applies 100 ms when the field is absent.

cases.case: MAC per mtch-SchedulingInfo (PTM DRX)
cases.what: mtch-SchedulingInfo and drx-ConfigPTM-List are not read; MAC only flags the LCID as MBS.

cases.case: Physical layer per mbs-SessionInfoList, searchSpaceMTCH and pdsch-ConfigMTCH
cases.what: G-RNTI PDCCH and PDSCH use the same search space 0 and PDSCH-ConfigCommon path as MCCH.

cases.case: SDAP entity per mbs-SessionId and indication to upper layers
cases.what: PDCP delivers straight to the IP interface; there is no SDAP entity and no indication.

cases.case: Receive DL-SCH with the g-RNTI
cases.what: Every advertised G-RNTI is searched each slot and its PDSCH decoded.

noted: Every session on MCCH is joined; there is no notion of the services the UE is interested in.
Received MTCH packets go to the same IP interface as unicast; up to three leading bytes before an IPv4 header are stripped, a mitigation the code labels as such.
The UE assumes 15 kHz subcarrier spacing (ten slots per frame) for MBS.

requirements.name: Broadcast MRB release

cases.case: Release PDCP, RLC and MAC configuration when a session leaves MCCH
cases.what: A G-RNTI missing from the new MCCH is removed from MAC and each of its MRBs has RLC, PDCP and the MAC LCID flag released.

cases.case: Release SDAP entity and indicate to upper layers
cases.what: No SDAP entity exists, so none is released and nothing is indicated.

noted: If two sessions use the same LCID, the second is not wired and releasing the first removes the MRB the second relies on.

requirements.name: MAC reception for MCCH and MTCH

cases.case: Downlink assignment for MCCH-RNTI and G-RNTI passed to HARQ
cases.what: MCCH-RNTI goes to the broadcast HARQ process and each G-RNTI to its own process.

cases.case: No HARQ acknowledgement for MCCH-RNTI or G-RNTI
cases.what: HARQ-ACK is generated only for C-RNTI grants.

cases.case: Retransmissions combined in the soft buffer
cases.what: Every grant is forced to be a new transmission, so a repetition of the same transport block is decoded alone rather than combined.

cases.case: Unconfigured LCID in a G-RNTI MAC PDU discarded
cases.what: G-RNTI PDUs share the unicast demultiplexer: an LCID not flagged as MBS goes to the unicast RLC (and into a DRB if one has that LCID), and a unicast SDU on a flagged LCID goes into the MRB.

cases.case: Logical channel identified by G-RNTI and LCID
cases.what: MRBs are keyed by LCID alone in MAC, RLC and PDCP.

cases.case: MTCH LCIDs 1 to 32 (Table 6.2.1-1c)
cases.what: Only LCIDs below 32 can be enabled for MBS, so LCID 32 cannot be received.

cases.case: Broadcast DRX per G-RNTI (clause 5.7a)
cases.what: No PTM DRX is applied; every G-RNTI is monitored in every slot, which is the behaviour the clause gives when no PTM DRX is configured.

noted: One downlink grant is kept per slot at the PHY, so a C-RNTI grant and a G-RNTI grant in the same slot overwrite each other.

cases.case: RX_Next_Highest from the first UMD PDU with an SN
cases.what: MRB entities set RX_Next_Highest from the first segmented PDU; complete SDUs are delivered directly.

cases.case: Entity release discards everything
cases.what: Release stops the entity and clears its receive window, SDU buffer and timer.

cases.case: RX_NEXT and RX_DELIV from the first received SN
cases.what: On the first PDU, RX_NEXT is set to the received COUNT plus one and RX_DELIV to it minus half the window, with the HFN chosen by the UE as the clause allows.

cases.case: No deciphering or integrity verification
cases.what: Security stays off for MRB entities; it is enabled only for SRB1 and DRB LCIDs.

cases.case: SIB21 stored
cases.what: The first SIB21 is stored and its FSAI counts logged; nothing acts on it.

cases.case: MBSInterestIndication
cases.what: The message and its UL-DCCH message class extension are not in the codec and the procedure is not implemented.

cases.case: MBS Interest Indication for broadcast reception on a non-serving cell (Release 18)
cases.what: The UE has no MBS Interest Indication, and its codec has neither nonServingCellMII in SIB1 nor the Release 18 extension of the message.

features.name: MBS multicast in the RAN
features.summary: Release 17 multicast (shared delivery to UEs in RRC_CONNECTED) and Release 18 multicast reception in RRC_INACTIVE are not implemented in the gNB or the UE; only codec types and a few placeholder fields exist.

requirements.name: NGAP multicast session management

cases.case: Distribution Setup
cases.what: No code sends DISTRIBUTION SETUP REQUEST.

cases.case: Distribution Release
cases.what: No code sends DISTRIBUTION RELEASE REQUEST.

cases.case: Multicast Session Activation
cases.what: The NGAP dispatcher has no case for the request; it is logged as unsupported.

cases.case: Multicast Session Deactivation
cases.what: No case for the request.

cases.case: Multicast Session Update
cases.what: No case for the request.

requirements.exists: The CU-CP records a multicast join or leave reported in a PDU Session Resource Setup or Modify request.

requirements.name: F1AP and E1AP multicast contexts

cases.case: F1AP Multicast Context Setup, Modification, Release and Release Request
cases.what: No F1AP multicast procedure exists on either peer.

cases.case: F1AP Multicast Group Paging and Multicast Distribution Setup/Release
cases.what: Not implemented.

cases.case: E1AP MC Bearer Context procedures
cases.what: Only the E1AP ID extraction helpers know the MC message types; no procedure exists.

cases.case: F1AP Release 18 multicast procedures: Multicast Context Notification, Multicast Common Configuration, MBS Multicast Configuration query
cases.what: Neither the procedures nor their messages are in the F1AP codec.

requirements.exists: A G-CS-RNTI field and setter in the DU session (never called) and a session type flag.

cases.case: Multicast MRB from dedicated RRC signalling
cases.what: No RRCReconfiguration path sets up a multicast MRB.

cases.case: DCI formats 4_1 and 4_2, G-CS-RNTI
cases.what: The DCI format list ends at 4_0 and there is no G-CS-RNTI type.

cases.case: Multicast MCCH acquisition in RRC_INACTIVE (Release 18)
cases.what: The UE has no multicast MCCH, no Multicast MCCH-RNTI and no MBSMulticastConfiguration message.

cases.case: Multicast MRB establishment in RRC_INACTIVE (Release 18)
cases.what: No path sets up a multicast MRB from MBSMulticastConfiguration.

cases.case: Multicast MCCH sent on PDCCH addressed to Multicast MCCH-RNTI
cases.what: The DU has no multicast MCCH and no Multicast MCCH-RNTI; its MCCH scheduler serves broadcast MCCH only.

cases.case: Multicast MCCH change notification
cases.what: Not implemented.

cases.case: MBSMulticastConfiguration in RRCRelease and on multicast MCCH
cases.what: The message is not in the RRC codec and no RRCRelease carries multicast configuration.
